This study examines the Rosenau equation, a nonlinear partial differential equation that models the propagation of shallow water waves in channels. We introduce a novel numerical approach utilizing the one-dimensional discontinuous Galerkin finite element method to solve this equation. The analysis provides rigorous error estimates for the proposed scheme, supported by numerical experiments that validate both the accuracy and the effectiveness of the method.

This paper investigates the stability of solution semigroups for a coupled PDE framework modeling the interaction between incompressible fluids and compressible fluids. The system comprises an incompressible Navier-Stokes set paired with compressible Navier equations, linked through a coupling mechanism involving the normal velocity at a shared interface. We establish that the resulting system matrix is boundedly invertible by employing a compatible variational framework and applying an inf-sup criterion. Consequently, this confirms the existence of a well-defined, holomorphic inf-sup constant for the semigroupe of solutions.

We present a theoretical investigation into the formation of interlayer exciton Wigner crystals (IXWC) within van der Waals heterostructures. By employing a model that accounts for the interplay between Coulomb interactions and the magnetic field, we demonstrate that the IXWC phase is stabilized by the magnetic field. Specifically, the phase boundary separating the IXWC and liquid exciton regimes is found to be linearly proportional to the magnetic field. Furthermore, we identify the IXWC phase as a robust candidate for experimental observation in systems comprising monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides.

This study introduces a relative calibration method for radial velocities (RVs) in LAMOST medium-resolution stellar spectra. The calibration process involves matching LAMOST spectra with those from the LAMOST-SDSS cross-matching sample to identify common absorption lines, which are then used to calculate wavelength shifts. These shifts are applied to correct the RVs of the LAMOST sample. The precision of the corrected sample was validated against the SDSS sample, achieving an accuracy of approximately 0.1 km s$^{-1}$ for stars with spectral types ranging from F to M. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the precision of RV calibration in LAMOST spectra is strongly influenced by the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and the spectral type of the target stars.

This study addresses the inverse scattering problem by determining the spatial distribution of the permittivity field from scattered electromagnetic data obtained across multiple frequencies and incident angles. We introduce a novel framework that utilizes a spherical harmonic expansion to represent both the permittivity field and the permittivity tensor, while employing an equivariant neural network to model the scattering operator. This approach offers a significant reduction in the number of required forward simulations, thereby enhancing computational efficiency. Additionally, we present a theoretical analysis of the scattering operator's properties, demonstrating that it is injective under specific conditions. These findings establish a theoretical basis for the unique reconstruction of the permittivity field from wide-band scattered electromagnetic measurements.

This study introduces a novel accelerated degradation model for two dependent diffusion processes, where the mean functions are linked through a linear relationship. The approach relies on the assumption that the initial states of these processes follow a bivariate gamma distribution, while the random effects exhibit a gamma distribution. This framework accommodates scenarios involving both positive and negative dependency. Parameter estimation utilizes the maximum likelihood method, and the associated Fisher information matrix is derived to evaluate the model's asymptotic properties. Furthermore, the paper proposes an optimal experimental design strategy for the model. The proposed methodology is applied to analyze data from a battery discharge experiment, and the findings are compared with existing models.

We investigate the triangular flow $v_3$ in Au+Au and Cu+Ag collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200$ GeV using the AMPT model, which incorporates a multiphase transport approach. Our analysis examines how $v_3$ varies with centrality and transverse momentum ($p_T$). We observe that the centrality dependence of $v_3$ in Au+Au collisions aligns with experimental data, whereas $v_3$ in Cu+Cu collisions is overestimated. Additionally, the $p_T$ dependence of $v_3$ in Au+Au collisions is underestimated at low $p_T$ but overestimated at high $p_T$. These discrepancies between our results and data for Cu+Cu collisions and high $p_T$ Au+Au systems are attributed to the model's inability to accurately describe the particle spectra in those specific regions.

This study examines the polytropic behavior of solar wind plasma during interactions between Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejections (ICMEs) and High-Speed Streams (HSSs). By analyzing data from the ACE and WIND spacecraft, we identified 11 ICME-HSS events occurring between 2010 and 2019. Our results indicate that the polytropic index ($\gamma$) for ICME plasma is consistently lower than that of HSS plasma. Specifically, the average polytropic index for ICMEs is $\langle\gamma\rangle = 1.05 \pm 0.05$, whereas for HSSs it is $\langle\gamma\rangle = 1.15 \pm 0.05$. These findings suggest that ICME plasma is more thermally compressible than HSS plasma. Additionally, we observed that the polytropic index for ICMEs increases with higher average solar wind speed, whereas no such trend exists for HSSs. We attribute the lower polytropic index in ICMEs to the presence of a substantial population of low-temperature plasma.

The Random Waypoint (RWP) model is a widely recognized approach for simulating mobile nodes, yet its stochastic properties have not been thoroughly examined in prior research. This paper addresses that gap by deriving the stationary distribution for RWP in a two-dimensional bounded area, demonstrating that it is uniform across the domain. Furthermore, we establish the model's autocorrelation function and its spectral density function, which are essential for analyzing the model's long-term behavior. Simulation results indicate that node velocity distributions are highly sensitive to the minimum speed threshold ($v_{min}$), whereas the stationary node density remains largely unaffected by velocity limits. Additionally, the study reveals that node positions exhibit a transient non-uniform distribution before converging to the model's stationary state.

This study examines $K^+K^-$ pairs within the STAR detector at RHIN, specifically analyzing the effective mass spectrum near $2m_K$ and transverse momentum ($p_T$) distribution. The analysis utilizes data from $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200$ GeV collisions recorded in 2007, 2008, and 2012. The $K^+K^-$ pair invariant mass distribution is modeled using a Gaussian function, while the $p_T$ distribution is fitted with a sum of two Gammas. The findings indicate that the effective mass spectrum and $p_T$ distribution for $K^+K^-$ pairs are consistent with those of uncorrelated $K^+K$ pairs. Additionally, the $K^+K^-$ pair effective mass spectrum is compared against the $K^0_S$ mass distribution.

The microscopic collective inertial mass, a fundamental element of the macroscopic Bohr Hamiltonian, is essential for calculating nuclear reaction cross sections. This paper introduces a new approach to computing the microscopic collective inertial mass for nuclear reactions, accounting for the effective in-medium mass of nucleons. We demonstrate that this mass exhibits significant sensitivity to the effective mass of nucleons, showing that it can be substantially reduced in scenarios involving strong effective mass suppression. Furthermore, we analyze the implications of these findings for nuclear reaction dynamics.

The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) serves as a benchmark for evaluating general-purpose AI systems. It consists of a vast collection of scenarios requiring the identification of patterns and the generation of solutions. While ARC tasks are designed to be accessible to humans, they remain challenging for current AI, making them ideal for investigating how such problems can be abstracted and solved. This paper introduces a novel approach to solving these tasks by utilizing graph-based representations of the images within the corpus. We demonstrate that this method can address a significant portion of the problems in the small ARC dataset. Furthermore, we examine the characteristics of these constructed graphs and outline a search-based framework for solving the instances.

This work examines the regularity properties of entropy solutions to scalar conservation laws featuring a discontinuous flux, specifically within a one-dimensional domain. The flux function is discontinuous along a curve that divides the domain into two regions, where each region is defined by a distinct flux function. We demonstrate that the trace of entropy solutions along this separating curve possesses fractional regularity. Furthermore, we establish that the regularity of these entropy solutions in a neighborhood adjacent to the curve is governed by the regularity of their traces on that interface.

This study presents the first measurement of the branching fractions for $B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{\mp} K^{\pm}$ and $B^{0} \to D_{s}^{-} K^{+}$, utilizing proton-proton collision data from the LHCb experiment recorded at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV with an integrated luminosity of 3.0 fb$^{-1}$. The observed branching fractions are determined to be $\mathcal{B}(B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{-} K^{+}) = (1.02 \pm 0.10 \pm 0.04) \times 10^{-4}$ and $\mathcal{B}(B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{+} K^{-}) = (1.02 \pm 0.10 \pm 0.04) \times 10^{-4}$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second is systematic. Additionally, the branching fraction for $B^{0} \to D_{s}^{-} K^{+}$ is measured as $(1.02 \pm 0.10 \pm 0.04) \times 10^{-4}$.

This study introduces a novel multcarrier-division-division duplex (MDD) framework designed for cell-free massive MIMO (CFmMIMO) systems. By utilizing a single radio frequency (RF) chain per remote radio unit (RRU), the architecture achieves a hardware cost reduction of 50% compared to traditional setups that employ two RF chains per RRU. The design ensures that the uplink and downlink transmit power spectra are perfectly complementary, thereby eliminating intercell interference. The paper derives the spectral efficiency (SE) for both CFmMIMO and conventional cellular massive MIMO (CSM) systems under MDD, subsequently comparing their performance. The analysis reveals that, despite having fewer RF chains, the CFmMIMO architecture delivers significantly higher spectral efficiency than CSM, particularly as the number of remote units increases.

Differentially private (DP) data analysis has gained significant traction in recent years, particularly within the shuffle model, where raw data is shuffled by trusted but non-seeing parties before being sent to an untrusted server. This paper investigates the shuffle model for estimating the mean of a real-valued function. We present a general framework that enables mean estimation with a tight accounting of the resulting DP noise, thereby eliminating the need for post-processing. This approach is versatile and can be applied to any existing DP algorithm for mean estimation. We demonstrate the efficacy of this framework by applying it to the Laplace mechanism, subsequently deriving a new algorithm for mean estimation that achieves a total error of $O(\sqrt{\frac{1}{\varepsilon n}})$, which represents a significant improvement over the prior best-known error bound of $O(\frac{1}{\varepsilon^2 n})$.

Orthogonal Time Frequency Multiplexing (OTFS) has emerged as a leading modulation scheme for future wireless systems, particularly in highly mobile environments. However, its reliance on the Wigner-Ville Distribution (WVD) for signal detection introduces significant computational complexity. This paper introduces a low-complexity receiver for OTS signals by proposing a novel modulation perspective that utilizes a time-domain basis set. This new framework, termed Orthogonal Time Sequency Multiplexing (OTSM), decomposes the OTSF signal into time-domain components, enabling the derivation of a low-complexity detector. Furthermore, the study investigates the performance of this proposed detector and establishes a closed-form expression for the bit error rate (BER) under Rayleigh fading conditions. Numerical simulations confirm that the derived BER expression aligns closely with simulation outcomes.

This study examines the operator norm within the Banach algebra of absolutely summable series on a discrete semigroup $G$ equipped with a weight $\omega$, specifically $\ell^1(G, \omega)$. We establish that the norm is determined by the supremum of the $\omega$-norms of all homomorphisms from $G$ into the unit circle. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the algebra's unit ball is weakly compact if and only if $\omega$ is bounded. Finally, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the algebra to possess the approximation property.

This study employs a two-dimensional axisymmetric numerical model to investigate the behavior of molten metal melt pools during laser spot melting. The model incorporates a moving heat source, fluid flow, and heat transfer, with the melt pool's shape defined by a moving free surface. The fluid flow is governed by the Navier-Stokes equations, solved via the finite element method, while the flow's physical properties are determined by surface tension gradients and the buoyancy force. The surface temperature is calculated using a combination of the Stefan and Planck laws. The results indicate that the melt pool's shape is influenced by laser power, beam spot size, and the material's surface tension coefficient. Additionally, the model predicts the formation of keyholes and provides a quantitative analysis of the melt pool's dimensions.

This study examines a wireless system designed for energy transfer and mobile edge computing (MEC) within public transport vehicles (PTVs), where PTV-mounted MEC servers assist connected electric buses. The system aims to maximize the total data rate of the MEC tasks executed on the bus while ensuring a minimum energy threshold for the bus. The optimization involves balancing the energy duration, and the resulting problem is formulated as a non-convex mixed integer fractional programming problem. The paper proposes a low-complexity algorithm to solve this challenge, utilizing the successive convex approximation method for the non-convex components and the Dinkelbach algorithm for the fractional terms. The study further demonstrates that incorporating intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) significantly enhances the system's performance.

The approximate degree of a function $f$ represents the least possible degree of a real polynomial $P$ that approximates $f$ to within an additive error of $\epsilon=1/3$. This measure is a fundamental component of quantum complexity theory, specifically in the study of bounded-error quantum query complexity. In this work, we establish that the approximate degree of any DNF or CNF formula $f$ is equivalent to the degree of its sensitivity polynomial, $sensitivity(f)$, up to a factor of at most $O(\log n)$. This result provides a significant advancement over the prior best bound of $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{d})$, where $d$ denotes the formula's depth. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the approximate degree of a DNF or CNF formula $f$ is bounded below by $\Omega(\sqrt{d})$, thereby extending the application of Nisan's classic polynomial identity to the domain of approximate degree analysis.

Bistability is a fundamental characteristic of numerous biological systems, including cellular signaling and gene regulatory networks. This paper introduces a computational approach for detecting bistable structures in nonlinear dynamical systems by leveraging the Conley index. The method is illustrated through two applications: first, it establishes a theoretical framework for identifying bistability in a simplified model of cellular signaling; second, it demonstrates the detection of bistable structures in a gene regulatory model using the Conley Network Toolbox.

This study examines the equation of state for spin-polarized strange quark matter under finite temperature and strong magnetic field conditions. We employ the MIT bag model to describe the system, incorporating the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model to account for quark interactions. Our results indicate that the magnetic field significantly influences the star's structure, causing the radius to decrease as the field strength increases. Furthermore, we observe that the star's mass rises with higher chiral chemical potential values.

The convergence of audio and video data has recently gained significant traction within the research community, driven by the potential to enhance machine intelligence through the fusion of multiple sensory modalities. This paper reviews recent breakthroughs in deep audio-visual correlation learning, with a specific focus on the challenges associated with aligning audio and video data temporally.

The Linear Ordering Problem (LOP) is a non-convex combinatorial optimization task that seeks to identify a permutation of a set of vertices satisfying specific constraints, with the goal of maximizing an objective function. This formulation is applicable to numerous real-world scenarios, including scheduling, ranking, and consensus building. However, solving LOP is NP-hard, meaning that finding an exact solution is computationally infeasible for large instances. Consequently, practitioners rely on heuristic methods to generate approximate results. This study introduces a probabilistic framework designed to evaluate the reliability of these LOP solutions. By modeling the problem within a probabilistic context, we derive the probability density function (PDF) for the objective function values and calculate the probability of failure. Furthermore, we propose a novel algorithm to estimate these failure probabilities. Extensive computational experiments were conducted to validate the proposed methodology.

This study investigates the impact of disorder on the superconducting phase diagram of NbN nanofilms by analyzing the critical current ($I_{c}$) and the zero-bias conductance ($G_{0}$) across varying temperatures and magnetic fields. The findings reveal that disorder significantly alters the phase diagram, particularly at low temperatures, where a complex interplay between superconductivity and a charge-density wave (CDW) state emerges. This state is characterized by a coexistence of $I_{c}$ and $G_{0}$, with the two parameters exhibiting an inverse correlation. We propose that this phenomenon arises from the competition between the superconducting state and the CDW state, with the latter being triggered by disorder.

Temporal graph databases are increasingly prevalent across various domains, including social networks, transportation, and biological systems. Temporal Regular Path Queries (TRPQs) serve as a crucial query language designed to retrieve paths adhering to specific patterns in such temporal graphs. This paper introduces a new temporal logic tailored for reasoning about these graphs, specifically designed to handle TRPQs. We demonstrate that answering TRPQs is equivalent to verifying formulas within this logic. Furthermore, we establish that the data complexity of evaluating temporal logic is equivalent to that of TRPQ evaluation, thereby validating the utility of our logic as a robust framework for reasoning about temporal graphs.

This study introduces a novel approach to decelerate free radicals by simultaneously employing Zeeman deceleration and radiofrequency Zeeman deceleration. The technique utilizes lithium atoms, which are produced via the photolysis of a lithium vapor cell, to generate a controlled mixture with cesium. This setup enables the efficient deceleration of free radicals, including the NO and NO$_2$ molecules, to terminal velocities reaching approximately 10 m/s.

The Swift satellite's X-ray Telescope (XRT) is capable of detecting a large number of X-ray transients, including gamma-ray bursts, X-ray novae, and supernovae. This study introduces a new, real-time transient detection system that utilizes the Swift data stream to identify and monitor these sources. The software is designed to operate in real-time, with the capability to run on a standard laptop. The authors have tested the software's performance using a six-month dataset from Swift-XRT, resulting in the discovery of 1,000 transients. The software is publicly available, and the associated catalogue of discovered transients is provided as a supplementary file.

We investigate the spin-1/2 $J_{1}$-$J_{2}$ XY model on a square lattice using the variational plaquette valence bond state (PVPVS) ansatz. This approach yields the ground state energy and the corresponding order parameter across the full range of $J_{1}$ and $J_{2}$ couplings. Our results indicate that the PVPVS ansatz accurately captures the ground state energy and order parameter, aligning closely with results from infinite Projected Entangled Pair State (iPEPS) simulations. Furthermore, we identify the plaquette valence bond ordering transition and determine the critical values of the $J_{1}$ and $J_{2}$ couplings.

This study introduces a three-dimensional panel data model designed to analyze bilateral trade flows. The approach decomposes these flows into distinct components: a fixed effect representing the pair of trading partners, a country-specific fixed effect, and a stochastic error term. By utilizing the residuals from this decomposition, the paper investigates the impact of trade agreements on bilateral trade. The results indicate that the proposed model offers superior performance compared to the traditional log-linear gravity model.

We investigate noncommutative $U(1)$ gauge theory in four dimensions, specifically examining the Moyal deformation of the field strength tensor $F_{\mu\nu}$. Our approach involves constructing the theory using the $L_\infty$ formalism, which allows us to derive the complete set of consistent interactions order by order in terms of the noncommutativity parameter $\theta$. Additionally, we demonstrate that this procedure yields a consistent theory of interacting abelian gauge fields that mirrors the original noncommutative formulation.

This study introduces a coherent equalization strategy for linear quantum systems, designed to counteract detrimental effects such as signal attenuation and noise introduced by channels. By synthesizing an equalizer that mirrors the underlying physics of the system, we leverage the inherent linearity to achieve coherent equalization. This approach offers a distinct advantage over traditional methods that merely amplify signal power, as it utilizes phase information to mitigate degradation without necessitating additional resources like extra power or increased bandwidth. We demonstrate the efficacy of this technique through the design of a frequency-compensation quantum equalizer, which successfully recovers attenuated signals within an optical fiber while conserving quantum states.

Perception of the passage of time is a dynamic psychological process that fluctuates based on an individual's mental and physical state. This study introduces a machine learning approach designed to forecast these temporal perceptions in real-time using wearable sensors. The system analyzes data from wearable devices to predict how long a user perceives a 10-second interval to last. The model was trained on a dataset comprising 1,000 participants, each performing 100 time-estimation trials. The results indicate that the model achieves a mean absolute error of 1.14 seconds, with an 80% accuracy rate in correctly classifying the passage of time perception. Furthermore, the model's performance is significantly enhanced by incorporating additional features such as heart rate variability, heart rate, and heart rate asymmetry. These findings suggest that the proposed method can serve as a valuable tool for the continuous, real-time monitoring of time perception, offering potential applications for assessing mental health and detecting early warning signs of mental disorders.

The growing influence of machine learning in critical sectors like healthcare and finance has intensified the debate over algorithmic fairness. While numerous fairness definitions have been proposed, their interrelationships remain poorly understood. This paper introduces a legal framework to evaluate and compare these definitions, specifically examining how they impact stakeholders' rights and obligations. We demonstrate that certain fairness concepts are mutually incompatible within this legal lens, thereby highlighting a critical challenge for the field.

We introduce a novel approach to detect the Majorana nature of neutrinos by utilizing lanthanoid trivalent ions. These ions are placed within a magnetic field and subjected to laser irradiation, facilitating transitions between their ground and excited states. The process involves the simultaneous emission of two neutrino pairs, which results in a measurable magnetization. This effect arises from an interference between different two-neutrino emission amplitudes, driven by the neutrino's intrinsic parity violation. The proposed scheme is designed to be compatible with current experimental setups.

This study investigates the binding energies of the lightest strangeness $S = -1$ and $S = -2$ hypernuclei ($S$-hyperons) with mass numbers $A=4$ to $7$ and $A=6$ to $5$, respectively, employing a phenomenological model grounded in chiral effective field theory. The framework relies on a two-body interaction between the $\Lambda$ and nucleons, calibrated using $\Lambda N$ scattering data and the binding energies of $A=4$ and $A=5$ hypernuclei. The resulting binding energies for $S$-hyperons align well with experimental results, with the model successfully predicting the binding energies of $A=6$ and $A=7$ hypernuclei. Additionally, the approach is extended to doubly strange hypernuclei, utilizing a two-body interaction between the $S$-hyperon and nucleons fitted to the binding energies of $A=4$ and $A=5$ systems. The calculated binding energies for $A=4$ to $7$ doubly strange hypernuclei show good agreement with experimental data for $A=4$ and $A=5$, while providing predictions for $A=6$ and $A=7$.

Social media platforms are frequently exploited to gather user data, often without their knowledge or explicit consent. This paper introduces MetaPriv, a privacy-centric browser extension designed to automatically manage user data collection on behalf of individuals. By utilizing machine learning, MetaPriv identifies the specific data points a website seeks and determines the optimal level of privacy protection for the user. It then autonomously enforces these privacy preferences on behalf of the user. Our findings indicate that MetaPriv successfully blocks 90% of data collection attempts while maintaining a seamless user experience.

This study examines the Hamiltonian-Cheeger (HC) model, a recently proposed framework for analyzing hypergraphs. The HC model extends the Ising model by assigning a spin value to each vertex, where these values correspond to the normalized Cheeger constants of all possible subgraphs containing a given number of vertices. We demonstrate that for a sufficiently large interaction parameter, the model exhibits Gibbs phase transitions characterized by an uncountable collection of Gibbs measures. This outcome arises from the model's inherent symmetry, which entails an infinite group of transformations acting on the spin values.

The LAMOST-DR7 central velocity catalog, derived from 110,000 galaxies, is presented in this paper. This catalog includes the central velocity ($V_{\rm c}$), the central velocity dispersion ($\sigma_{\rm c}$), and the central velocity dispersion error ($\sigma_{\rm c, err}$) for each galaxy. The $V_{\rm c}$ and $\sigma_{\rm c}$ values were derived from the integrated spectrum of each galaxy using the ETCHELLE pipeline, while the error estimate for $\sigma_{\rm c}$ was calculated using the method proposed by Cappellari et al. (2017). The catalog's completeness is estimated at 80% for galaxies with a central velocity dispersion exceeding $100\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$. Additionally, the paper provides a detailed analysis of the $V_{\rm c}$ and $\sigma_{\rm c}$ distributions, along with the $M_{\rm B}-\sigma_{\rm c}$ relation, for the LAMOST-DR7 galaxy sample.

This study introduces a new implementation of analytic response within the relativistic coupled-cluster framework, specifically tailored for coupled-cluster singles and pairs (CCS) and coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CCSD) theories. The primary objective is to calculate analytic derivatives of the energy, enabling the computation of properties like isotope shifts and polarizabilities. The method's validity is confirmed through calculations on the indium atom, yielding results that align with those from non-analytic methods. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the analytic approach offers a substantial performance advantage over traditional methods.

A collection of distinct elements, selected from each row of an $m \times n$ matrix with unique entries such that no two elements share the same column, is known as a *transversal*. This paper introduces a simple criterion that determines when a matrix possesses a transversal composed of $m$ distinct entries.

The proliferation of mobile devices with diverse display capabilities and network conditions has necessitated the transcode of video streams to match specific user requirements. This study examines the performance of transcoding services deployed in the cloud, specifically focusing on the impact of varying configurations of processing nodes. We evaluate how different node types—specifically those with differing processor speeds and memory capacities—affect service metrics such as response time, throughput, and availability. Our findings indicate that while faster processors and larger memory allocations yield superior performance, they also incur higher costs. To address this trade-off, we propose a cost-performance model that identifies optimal node configurations for specific service levels of agreement (SLAs).

This paper examines the number of cycles within random permutations, specifically focusing on achieving precise large deviations results for moderate deviation sequences. By utilizing novel techniques derived from combinatorial analysis, we derive a Laplace-type asymptotic for probabilities concerning cycle counts under increasingly intense deviation conditions.

This work demonstrates that the ground state solution of the energy supercritical Gross--Pitaevskii equation possesses a momentum index of zero. This conclusion follows from the established fact that such a ground state is stationary, combined with recent findings by the author and J. Zhang [1] indicating that any ground state of the same equation must have an actual Morse index of zero.

This study introduces a rigorous framework for the assessment of automated designs, specifically aimed at managing Type I error rates. The methodology employs a two-stage testing procedure: the initial stage involves a significance test to determine if a design is effective, while the second stage involves a confidence interval to estimate the magnitude of that effect. The paper outlines the specific conditions required for this framework to maintain strong control over Type I error rates. Furthermore, it provides a formal definition of a "valid automated design" and illustrates the approach through examples drawn from the automated medical image analysis field.

The metaverse, a persistent virtual ecosystem, is poised to transform how we interact with digital content. While current virtual reality (VR) applications are limited to isolated, individual experiences, the metaverse aims to enable immersive, shared, and collaborative digital encounters. However, rendering these complex, shared environments presents significant hurdles, particularly regarding the massive computational resources required for high-fidelity graphics. This paper introduces Distributed Hybrid Rendering (DHR), a new framework designed to facilitate high-quality, shared metaverse experiences. DHR leverages a hybrid approach that combines local and remote rendering techniques, utilizing a specialized algorithm to dynamically allocate rendering tasks between client devices and edge servers. This dynamic allocation ensures optimal performance tailored to varying network conditions and client capabilities. We validate DHR through a comprehensive simulation study, evaluating its effectiveness across diverse client configurations and network environments. The results demonstrate that DHR delivers superior performance compared to existing methods, successfully supporting high-quality, shared metaverse interactions.

This study investigates the impact of annotation and alignment accuracy on the performance evaluation of algorithms for complex orchestral music. We established a dataset featuring three levels of alignment precision: exact, rough, and no alignment. Performance comparisons were conducted using two methods: a standard Euclidean distance metric and a novel approach based on a Hamming distance applied to a vector representation of musical features. Results indicate that even minor annotation errors significantly degrade comparative outcomes, with the new Hamming distance metric demonstrating greater robustness against alignment inaccuracies compared to traditional Euclidean distance.

Full-duplex radios, which enable simultaneous transmission and reception, are poised to transform wireless communications by boosting spectral efficiency and reducing latency. However, the inherent challenge of self-interference (SI) remains a significant hurdle. This paper introduces a new framework for self-interference cancellation (SIxC) in full-duplex systems, integrating both multi-element arrays and advanced digital signal processing. The proposed method utilizes a hybrid approach that combines a low-resolution analog network with a high-resolution digital component, effectively addressing the distinct characteristics of near-field and far-field interference. Simulation results demonstrate that this technique achieves an 80 dB reduction in self-interference, thereby enabling the practical deployment of full-duplex wireless systems.

The consolidation of colloidal droplets is a critical process in the pharmaceutical sector, where it is widely used to manufacture liquid-filled capsules. This study investigates the buckling and invagination mechanisms occurring during droplet consolidation. We demonstrate that the morphology of the resulting capsules is governed by the interplay between the droplet's surface tension and the elasticity of the surrounding elastic film. By analyzing the buckling and invagination dynamics, we establish that the process is driven by the competition between the elastic film's resistance and the droplet's surface tension. Furthermore, we propose a theoretical model that accurately predicts the critical volume required for buckling and the final capsule shape. This model relies on the assumption that buckling and invagination occur in a two-stage process: first, the droplet undergoes buckling, followed by the elastic film's stretching and subsequent invagination. This two-phase framework successfully explains the observed experimental phenomena.

Lyman-alpha (Ly$\alpha$) emission from protoplanetary disks (PPDs) has been observed in numerous young stellar objects (YSOs), yet the underlying mechanisms driving this radiation remain unclear. We propose that the Ly$\alpha$ flux originates from the fluorescence of atomic hydrogen within the PPDs. By modeling the Ly$\alpha$ emission from a disk of varying inclination angles, we demonstrate that the observed flux is primarily governed by the disk's gas surface density and the strength of the stellar radiation field. Our results indicate that the Ly$\alpha$ luminosity scales with the square of the gas surface density, suggesting that the Ly$\alpha$ luminosity-to-disk-mass ratio serves as a reliable tracer for disk mass. Furthermore, we find that the Ly$\alpha$ luminosity-to-disk-mass ratio correlates with the stellar X-ray luminosity, implying that the Ly$\alpha$ luminosity can be predicted based on the stellar X-ray luminosity and disk mass. We also explore the impact of disk inclination on Ly$\alpha$ luminosity, finding that the Ly$\alpha$ luminosity is significantly reduced for highly inclined disks. Finally, we discuss the implications of our findings for the study of PPDs and the interpretation of Ly$\alpha$ observations.

This paper introduces a fingerprint-based millimeter wave (mWave) positioning framework enhanced by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). The proposed system utilizes an RIS to generate multiple line-of-sight (LoS) paths, which are subsequently fingerprinted to determine the user's location. A comprehensive channel model is developed to analyze the impact of the RIS on the LoS path loss and shadowing effects. Furthermore, a methodology for constructing fingerprints from these LoS components is presented, followed by an analysis of the resulting positioning accuracy. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that the system achieves superior positioning precision compared to scenarios lacking an RIS.

This study examines the generation of twisted particles within magnetic fields, specifically focusing on the creation of electron-positron pairs in the fields of magnetars and black holes. We demonstrate that the topological twist of these pair particles is governed by the field's inhomogeneity. Furthermore, we analyze twisted pair production in the context of black hole accretion disks, determining that the resulting toroidal currents can significantly influence the dynamics of the disk.

The surge in electric vehicle (EV) adoption is driving a significant expansion in charging infrastructure, yet this expansion presents complex challenges for both utilities and vehicle owners. Utilities must integrate this new load into the grid, while owners must select charging options that fit their specific needs. This paper addresses these issues by examining the optimal placement of chargers, pricing strategies, and market design. We begin by developing a framework to determine the ideal number and location of chargers, factoring in both EV demand and the cost of electricity generation and transmission. Subsequently, we introduce a pricing model that accounts for the time-of-value of electricity to the grid, ensuring that charging costs reflect their actual economic impact. Finally, we propose a market design that enables EV owners to trade charging capacity with other users. Collectively, these frameworks offer valuable insights for policymakers, utilities, and investors navigating the EV charging sector.

This paper examines the optimal allocation of treatments in a two-arm clinical trial where some participants receive both (double-don) and others receive only one, utilizing a generalized response variable. We demonstrate that a specific two-stage, completely randomized design—where the first stage assigns treatments based on a randomized threshold and the second stage randomizes the remaining sample within each group—is optimal. This method extends the well-known "response-adaptive" designs, which typically involve binary assignments, to scenarios involving both groups. We further introduce a straightforward, non-iterative algorithm for implementing this design. Finally, we provide a simulation study that contrasts this approach with standard designs, highlighting its superior ability to maximize information gain.

We have derived general formulas for the three-point functions of arbitrary current multiplets in a unitary, superconformal theory with ${\mathcal N}=1$ symmetry. These formulas are fully determined by the conformal dimensions and R-symmetry charges of the multiplet constituents. Furthermore, we have calculated the three-point functions for arbitrary multiplets involving half-integer spins, which are completely fixed by the conformal dimensions and R-charges of the constituent fields.

Machine learning is increasingly ubiquitous in daily life, yet the field of Machine Teaching remains largely unexplored regarding its potential for educational applications. This study examines the use of Machine Teaching as a pedagogical instrument to educate children about machine learning. We introduce a novel framework designed to teach both basic machine learning concepts and the underlying machine teaching principles to young audiences. The system is built upon a curated dataset of images depicting everyday objects, such as animals and food, and includes two interactive modules: a Machine Teaching interface and a Machine Learning interface. The teaching module allows users to select training examples and parameters to customize a learner, while the learning module enables users to test their models against novel instances. We evaluated this system with 12 children aged 10 to 12 years, assessing their ability to understand machine learning principles and acquire knowledge about machine teaching through the platform. The results indicate that the system is effective in helping children grasp machine learning concepts and learn about machine teaching.

This paper examines the integration of continual learning within the reinforcement learning (RL) domain. We investigate how to design RL agents capable of acquiring new skills across multiple tasks while retaining prior knowledge. Our analysis covers the advantages of this approach, the specific challenges it entails, and potential strategies for resolution. Additionally, we introduce a novel benchmark suite for continual RL, comprising a selection of tasks from the OpenAI Gym library.

Photonic quantum information is typically transmitted across optical fibers using polarization or orbital angular momentum (OAM) degrees of freedom (DOFs). However, OAM signals cannot propagate over long distances, whereas polarization is restricted in its information capacity. Consequently, converting between these modes is vital for advancing quantum communication. This study demonstrates the coherent translation of quantum information from OAM to polarization and vice versa within an integrated silicon nitride chip. This is achieved by employing a spatial light modulator to generate OAM photons and directing them into the chip, where an on-chip spiral phase plate (SPP) performs the spatial-to-polarization conversion. The resulting photonic quantum state is then read out via its polarization properties using a single-photon detector. The successful demonstration of this coherent conversion paves the way for more efficient quantum information processing and transmission.

This study examines the influence of base pair mismatches on electron transport within DNA. We introduce a quantum mechanical framework for electron transport in DNA that incorporates the physical characteristics of nucleobases, the sugar-phosphate backbone, and the effects of base stacking. Using the quantum master equation, we calculate the electrical current as a function of applied bias voltage, specifically analyzing the impact of single mismatches located at various positions. Our findings indicate that minor mismatches cause only slight deviations in current, whereas significant mismatches trigger pronounced anomalies. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the current profile for a double mismatch resembles the superposition of the current profiles for two isolated single mismatches.

Accurate registration of multi-view point clouds is essential for 3D reconstruction and object recognition. While the Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm is a widely used standard, it often struggles with local minima, resulting in suboptimal alignments. To address this, we introduce a new method that integrates K-means clustering with ICP. This approach clusters points from the source view into groups based on their spatial distribution and then aligns each group with its corresponding cluster in the target view. By operating on these smaller subsets, the method significantly reduces the risk of converging to local minima, thereby enhancing both the speed and robustness of the registration process. Experimental results demonstrate that our technique surpasses traditional ICP implementations in accuracy and efficiency.

We report on the magnetic structure of Tb$_3$Ru$_7$O$_{12}$, a compound featuring alternating-bond Ru$^{3+}$ chains with a spin-3/2 configuration, embedded within a non-uniform internal magnetic field generated by Tb$^{3+}$ ions. This system exhibits a complex magnetic phase diagram characterized by three distinct transitions: a primary transition at $T_{\rm c1} \approx 10$ K, a secondary one at $T_{\rm c2} \approx 0.5$ K, and a third at $T_{\rm c3} \approx 0.1$ K. While neutron diffraction data indicate that the primary transition at $T_{\rm c1}$ corresponds to the ordering of Tb$^{3+}$ moments into a non-collinear, non-uniform antiferromagnetic state, the subsequent transitions at $T_{\rm c2}$ and $T_{\rm c3}$ are attributed to the ordering of Ru$^{3+}$ moments. Specifically, the transition at $T_{\rm c2}$ marks the onset of a partially disordered state, where Tb$^{3+}$ moments are already ordered, while Ru$^{3+}$ moments order only partially. This study examines the fundamental optimality conditions for constrained mathematical programming problems where both the objective and constraint functions are DC (difference of convex) mappings. By utilizing the concept of subgradients derived from these convex components, we introduce a new set of necessary optimality conditions termed "subgradients optimality conditions." The paper further explores the relationship between our proposed conditions and the traditional Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, demonstrating that KKT conditions are strictly more restrictive than the subgradient conditions. Additionally, we establish necessary and sufficient KKT conditions within the specific context of semidefinite programming.

We introduce domain collisions as a novel mechanism for generating domain wall networks within expanding cosmological spacetimes. This process occurs when oppositely oriented domain walls encounter one another, resulting in a persistent domain wall network. We demonstrate that domain wall networks formed through collisions exhibit distinct characteristics compared to those produced by standard mechanisms. Specifically, we analyze the evolution of domain wall networks in a flat Friedmann-Robertson-Walker universe, focusing on both the scaling and non-scaling regimes. Our findings indicate that collision-derived networks are non-scaling and display a significantly greater abundance of network intersections relative to traditionally formed networks.

Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) has proven highly effective for robotic control, yet it typically demands extensive training time and often fails to generalize across different tasks. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel Bayesian controller fusion approach that integrates multiple neural network policies. This method enables the system to leverage diverse control priors, such as expert demonstrations, to enhance sample efficiency and adaptability. We evaluate the approach on a simulated quadruped robot tasked with navigating an obstacle course. Experimental results indicate that our proposed fusion method outperforms standard RL techniques, particularly in terms of sample efficiency.

Accurate stroke perfusion analysis is essential for effective diagnosis and treatment planning. This paper introduces a differentiable deconvolution method that leverages end-to-end training to enhance perfusion analysis. By utilizing the PyTorch framework, we achieve a differentiable implementation of the standard deconvolution approach. Experimental results indicate that our technique produces more precise perfusion parameter estimates and offers greater robustness against noise.

We present the first calculation of the zero-jettiness beam function at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N$^3$LO) in QCD perturbation theory. This achievement marks the completion of the full NN$^3$LO computation for the 0-jettiness variable, a critical observable utilized in numerous high-precision phenomenological studies.

This paper investigates the properties of the power graph and prime power power subgraph associated with a finite group $G$. We demonstrate that for a finite group $G$, the power graph $\mathcal{P}(G)$ is chordal if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to the trivial group, the cyclic group of order $2$, or the symmetric group $S_2$.

This study introduces a new method for separating target sources from noisy mixtures by training on artificially generated optimal mixtures. This approach is particularly advantageous when optimal examples of the target source are scarce. We demonstrate that the resulting separation quality is equivalent to what would be achieved using an unlimited supply of real target source mixtures. This performance parity is accomplished by training on significantly fewer real source samples. The method is highly effective for scenarios where target source material is limited, such as in speaker diarization or isolating specific voices.

The concept of coherence in quantum information theory refers to the presence of superpositions. In this work, we broaden this definition to identify a state as coherent relative to an arbitrary measurement apparatus whenever it yields indistinguishable outcomes across all possible measurements. We demonstrate that the resulting class of coherent states is substantially broader than those linked to standard basis vectors, yet we establish that the extreme points within this set correspond precisely to pure states diagonal relative to the measurement's elements. Furthermore, we outline a method for quantifying the degree of coherence in a state, proving its robustness against decoherence processes induced by specific measurement strategies.

We present a detailed analysis of Type C Quasi-Periodic Oscillations (CQPOs) observed in H 1743–322, a recurrent black hole X-ray binary, utilizing data from the 2012–2013 outbursts recorded by the Swift-XRT and NICER instruments. Our investigation reveals that the CQPOs in these events are characterized by a broad range of periods, spanning from 0.1 to 1.0 seconds, and exhibit a complex, multi-component structure. We observe a distinct correlation between the CQPO periods and the source's X-ray luminosity, a relationship that aligns with the hypothesis that these modulations arise from the Lense-Thirring precession of the inner accretion disk. Furthermore, the data indicate that the precession period remains consistent across multiple outbursts, suggesting that the black hole's spin is invariant. We also note a correlation between the CQPO periods and the source's inclination angle, which supports the idea that the accretion disk is tilted relative to the black hole's spin axis.

This paper introduces an open-domain question answering (QA) system designed to address the challenges of answering complex, multi-part inquiries within the e-Governance sector. We present a novel QA framework that integrates a question decomposition module, a retrieval system, and a generation model. This system is designed to handle queries of varying complexity, ranging from single-part to multi-part questions. Our approach was evaluated on a new dataset specifically created for the e-Governance domain, and the results demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art performance in this field.

The EAGLE cosmological hydrodynamical simulations have successfully replicated numerous observed properties of the local galaxy population, including the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, the stellar mass function, and the stellar mass–halo mass relationship. This strong agreement with data suggests that the simulations have correctly accounted for baryons. However, the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation is typically applied only to galaxies with masses below $10^{10} M_{\odot}$, leaving the baryonic inventory of more massive galaxies unaccounted for. This study investigates the baryonic content of galaxies exceeding $10^{10} M_{\odot}$ within the EAGLE framework. We find that the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation holds for galaxies with virial velocities greater than $100$ km/s, implying that the baryonic content of galaxies with masses above $10^{10} M_{\odot}$ is dominated by hot gas. Furthermore, the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation is consistent with the baryonic content of the Milky Way, indicating that the baryonic content of the Milky Way is dominated by hot gas. A subset $S$ of a graph $G$'s vertices is defined as a $k$-separator if removing $S$ divides $G$ into components where no two vertices in $S$ are adjacent, and each component contains at most $k$ vertices of $G$. Such a $k$-separator is termed "leftmost" if no other $k$-separator exists that is adjacent to it. This paper introduces a novel algorithm capable of enumerating all $k$-separators in a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. The approach achieves a runtime of $O(nm^{k+1} + n^{k+2})$ and a space complexity of $O(n^{k+1})$. Furthermore, the authors demonstrate that this algorithm can be adapted to identify all leftmost $k$-separators. The resulting time and space complexities for this adaptation are $O(n^{k+2} + m^{k+2})$ and $O(n^{k+1})$, respectively.

The reconfigurable wireless network (RWN) is a promising technology designed to meet the stringent requirements of emerging applications. However, the inherent complexity of the RWN environment, combined with the need to balance multiple Quality of Service (QoS) parameters, makes designing an optimal scheduler for these networks a challenging task. To address this, we introduce an actor-critic learning-based QoS-aware scheduler for RWNs. This approach utilizes actor-critic algorithms to learn an optimal scheduling policy, while also incorporating a prediction module to anticipate the QoS state in the subsequent time slot. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art solutions.

We introduce a novel approach to Quality Estimation (QE) designed to assist human post-editors (PE) by forecasting the effort required to correct machine translation output. Unlike traditional QE methods that evaluate entire translations as single units, our proposed method assesses quality at the individual word level. This granular perspective enables the system to identify specific problematic segments, thereby offering PE targeted suggestions for corrections. This study details the design of our method, outlines the necessary adjustments to existing models, and presents experimental results demonstrating the system's effectiveness.

This study investigates the potential of using observational data from black hole shadows to determine the value of the cosmological constant. We demonstrate that the cosmological constant can be uniquely determined from the shadow's shape and size, as well as from the apparent horizon locations of a Kerr--de Sitter spacetime. Furthermore, we analyze how the size and morphology of the shadow depend on the cosmological constant, the black hole's mass, and its spin. Our findings indicate that for a fixed cosmological constant, the shadow size decreases as the black hole mass increases, whereas an increase in the cosmological constant leads to a larger shadow size. Additionally, we explore how the shadow's size and shape vary with changes in the cosmological constant, the black hole's spin, and its mass. We observe that a higher spin results in a smaller shadow, while a larger black hole mass produces a larger shadow. Finally, we note that the shadow's shape remains relatively stable across variations in the cosmological constant, the black hole's spin, and its mass.

This study introduces a novel framework for solving relativistic hydrodynamic equations in two-dimensional Cartesian coordinates, designed to facilitate the investigation of relativistic fluid dynamics in astrophysical contexts. The work examines the evolution of a perfect fluid, incorporating a stress-energy tensor that integrates pressureless dust, an ideal fluid, and a cosmological constant. The proposed formulation relies on a new set of variables that are conformally invariant, thereby eliminating the need for the Lorentz boost step typically required in Cartesian systems. The authors demonstrate that these equations can be expressed using a 2+1 dimensional 3+1 decomposition, which facilitates the application of established numerical techniques. The reliability of this approach is validated through tests involving the expansion of a 2D box, the dynamics of a 2D vortex, and the evolution of a 1D shock wave.

This study examines the $D^{*+} K^0_{\rm S}$ and $D^{*0} K^+$ decay modes of $D^+_{sJ}$ mesons, utilizing the full LHCb dataset of $1.0\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ of $pp$ collisions. The analysis identifies two resonances in the $D^{*}K$ system, designated as $D^{*}_{sJ}(2317)^+$ and $D^{*}_{sJ}(2457)^+$, with masses and widths consistent with prior measurements. The $D^{*}_{sJ}(2317)^+$ is observed to decay into both $D^{*0}K^+$ and $D^{*+}K^0_{\rm S}$ channels, whereas the $D^{*}_{sJ}(2457)^+$ is detected exclusively in the $D^{*0}K^+}$ mode.

This paper introduces a novel class of fractal polynomials constructed on the Sierpiński gasket, a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$. The $n$-th degree polynomials within this class are determined by the $n$-th fractal Fourier coefficients of a specific function space. We demonstrate that these polynomials are unique and provide a closed-form expression for their $L^2$-norm. Additionally, we derive an explicit formula for the polynomials' gradient and calculate the $L^2$-norm of the gradient for an arbitrary function belonging to the relevant Sobolev space.

This study introduces a novel framework for visually grounded question generation that integrates both image and textual cues. Our approach employs a dual encoder-decoder architecture where the encoder processes visual inputs and a specific text embedding, while the decoder utilizes a recurrent attention mechanism to generate queries. Crucially, we implement a guiding strategy that leverages the decoder's attention weights to steer question generation, thereby enhancing the model's capacity to capture key visual elements. Comprehensive experiments across three datasets demonstrate that this guidance method yields significant performance gains over baseline models.

The cusp-core controversy remains a significant unresolved issue in astrophysics. While the standard view attributes the transformation from a density cusps to a flat core within dark matter halos to the gravitational influence of supernovae (SNe) ejecta, this study critically examines that mechanism. We demonstrate that the efficiency of this proposed transformation is highly sensitive to the initial density slope of the dark matter halo. Specifically, the transformation is only feasible for halos with an initial slope shallower than -1.2. Furthermore, the transformation is hindered by the presence of baryonic matter. We also argue that the transformation is unlikely to occur in halos with masses below 10^10 M_sun. Consequently, the conventional SN-driven explanation fails to account for the cusp-core controversy.

This work introduces a higher-order resolution calculus capable of removing both $\lambda$-abstractions and universal quantifiers. The system is inspired by first-order resolution calculi, notably superposition and E-resolution, and incorporates a heuristic for generating higher-order superpositions. We demonstrate the method's efficacy through extensive experiments on a range of benchmarks.

This study examines the replicator dynamics of two-population games, specifically focusing on cases where the strategic order is maintained. We demonstrate that the system's long-term behavior is governed by the symmetry of the strategy-ordered response function. Specifically, the model exhibits a stable polymorphic equilibrium when the response function displays even symmetry, whereas odd symmetry results in a stable monomorphic equilibrium.

This paper establishes the asymptotic normality of multivariate random forest estimators, which are capable of handling multiple response variables. We derive a central limit theorem for these estimators, providing a basis for constructing confidence intervals and conducting hypothesis tests. The proof utilizes the Lindeberg-Feller theorem, with simulation studies included to validate the results.

This study introduces a novel, decentralized algorithm designed to resolve the Electric Vehicle (EV) charging allocation challenge within unbalanced distribution grids. The core objective is to minimize the total cost of charging across all Electric Vehicles while adhering to power flow constraints and ensuring that both the EVs and the grid operate within their respective power limits. The proposed approach, termed Communication-Censored ADMM (CC-ADMM), leverages a specific communication topology to coordinate EV charging schedules. By integrating a probabilistic communication model, CC-ADMM significantly reduces the frequency of inter-agent communication, thereby lowering the associated communication overhead. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that CC-ADMM converges to the optimal solution with a rate of $\mathcal{O}(1/k)$, where $k$ represents the iteration count. Furthermore, the authors establish that the CC-ADMM framework is applicable to a broader class of optimization problems characterized by a specific structure. Extensive simulations were conducted to validate the algorithm's effectiveness and to evaluate the benefits of incorporating a probabilistic communication model.

The structural, elastic, and electronic properties of the orthorhombic perovskite $SmFeO_3$ were investigated using the GGA+U method. The study examined the material's stability, phase transitions, and elastic characteristics. Results indicate that the calculated lattice parameters align well with experimental data. Furthermore, the calculated elastic constants were compared with available experimental values, demonstrating strong agreement. The material was found to be mechanically stable, as evidenced by the satisfaction of the Born-Huang criteria. Additionally, the calculated bulk modulus, shear modulus, and Young's modulus were determined, along with the Poisson's ratio. The electronic structure analysis revealed that the $SmFeO_3$ compound exhibits semiconducting behavior.

Bacterial populations are highly diverse, with individual cells exhibiting distinct phenotypes that vary in their capacity to survive and reproduce. This diversity is driven by both genetic differences and environmental factors, which can induce shifts in gene expression and protein levels. Consequently, the resulting phenotypic variation influences the fitness of bacterial cells, a process that is often regulated by gene expression noise. This study investigates the phenotypic diversity of *Escherichia coli* by analyzing the fitness effects of mutations in the *rpoS* gene, which controls the general stress response. We demonstrate that the phenotypic variation in *rpoS* mutants is significantly greater than in wild-type strains, a finding that is strongly correlated with the magnitude of gene expression noise. Furthermore, we show that the fitness effects of these mutations are context-dependent, varying based on the specific phenotypic state of the cells. These results offer new insights into the mechanisms underlying phenotypic diversity in bacteria and its impact on evolutionary trajectories.

This paper introduces a data-driven approach to modeling the ventilation component of a smart building's HVAC infrastructure. The study utilizes extensive datasets from a real-world smart building to develop a data-driven model for the ventilation sector. This model is then integrated into a comprehensive smart building model, which is validated against actual operational data. The resulting framework offers significant potential for applications such as anomaly detection, system diagnostics, and the optimization of energy consumption.

We present a quantum version of the Stoner-Wohlfarth model designed for two-dimensional single-domain magnets, incorporating quantum fluctuations to determine the average magnetization and energy spectrum. By employing a method that integrates the exact ground state with a perturbative approach, we derive the average magnetization and subsequently calculate the total energy. Our analysis reveals that the resulting phase diagram is highly sensitive to quantum fluctuations, which induce a significant reduction in the coercive field. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the thermal-to-quantum crossover temperature is exceptionally low, effectively vanishing in the thermodynamic limit.

The primary objective of this study is to develop a novel dependency parsing framework that integrates insights from visual perception. We contend that the human brain's visual processing mechanisms can be translated into a robust strategy for identifying syntactic structures within text. To this end, we introduce a new model that merges a transformer-based language model with a graph attention network, designed to capture visual cues such as proximity and alignment. Furthermore, we propose a specific set of proximity and alignment features derived from the model's outputs, which are utilized to learn position-dependent graph attention parameters. Empirical evaluations on English and Chinese datasets demonstrate that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance.

Feature attribution methods are widely utilized to explain machine learning model predictions. Although these methods are predominantly evaluated on input spaces (eassistant: images), they are often applied to intermediate representations derived from the input. This study proposes a new framework for assessing these techniques directly in the image domain. We demonstrate that this approach offers a more intuitive evaluation of attribution methods by enabling the direct visualization of generated images. Furthermore, we propose a novel image-domain metric for quantifying the importance of latent features. Our comprehensive experiments evaluate various attribution methods using both existing and new image-domain metrics. Our results indicate that while some methods perform well on inputs, others excel when evaluated on intermediate representations. Finally, we introduce a new attribution method designed to operate within the image domain.

This study examines the linearization stability of thin-shell wormholes situated in the double-shadows region of the Reissner-Nordstr\"om spacetime, where reflection symmetry is broken. We demonstrate that the linear shell's dynamic evolution can be modeled as a one-degree-of-freedom system. Furthermore, we derive the stability criteria for both static and oscillatory wormholes, revealing that the violation of the null energy condition is essential for stabilizing any wormhole.

We establish a new inequality linking the Shannon entropy of random permutations to the entropy of their cycle structures. This result extends known entropy bounds regarding random walks to previously unexplored scenarios. Our proof technique relies on generating functions and combinatorial analysis, leveraging established findings from the theory of Brownian motion.

A trimer consists of three connected vertices within the triangular lattice. This paper examines the problem of identifying the largest possible trimer cover for such a grid, specifically focusing on the subset of configurations that achieve maximum density. We conclude by listing twenty challenging open problems, many of which are formulated specifically to address gaps in our current understanding.

Domain adaptation addresses the challenge of adapting a model trained on a source domain to perform effectively on a target domain. While most existing methods rely on aligning feature representations, they often overlook the alignment of the decision boundaries between source and target classifiers. This paper introduces a new approach that simultaneously aligns both the feature representations and the decision boundaries. Specifically, we propose learning a set of prototype classifiers and reciprocal points to capture the decision boundaries of both source and target domains. Furthermore, we develop a new loss function designed to align these classifiers and points across domains. Extensive experiments on various cross-domain classification tasks demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques.

This study introduces a method for estimating vehicle poses and reconstructing 3D models from stereo images. The approach utilizes a pre-trained deep learning model to detect vehicles and segment their 2D silhouettes. These silhouettes are then mapped to 3D space using a probabilistic shape prior, which is constructed from a collection of manually annotated vehicle datasets. The pose estimation process involves optimizing the 3D parameters to minimize the discrepancy between projected and detected silhouette contours. The system's performance was evaluated on the KITTI dataset, and the results demonstrate that this method achieves superior accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This paper introduces a new approach to generating query graphs for answering complex questions over knowledge graphs. The method employs a hierarchical structure that breaks down intricate queries into smaller, manageable sub-graphs. The generation process occurs in two phases: first, outlining the query by creating a high-level graph that identifies the primary knowledge domains required, and second, filling in the details by constructing specific query sub-graphs for each outline element. This two-phase strategy allows for the creation of complex queries that are both computationally efficient and semantically accurate. Empirical results demonstrate that this hierarchical method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both the semantic correctness and the efficiency of the generated queries.

This study introduces a novel algebraic structure based on polynomials featuring composite operators, with the set of polynomials containing a fixed common factor and those with coefficient sets restricted to specific subfields both confirming it as that. The work further demonstrates that these common-factor polynomials form a submonoid within the composite monoid, with applications explored in coding theory and cryptography.

Named entity recognition (NER) involves identifying entities within text and assigning them specific labels, a process that is often complicated by the fact that a single mention may correspond to multiple real-world entities. While traditional methods typically address static documents, modern applications require handling continuous, high-volume data streams. This paper presents a benchmark for evaluating named entity disambiguation techniques in streaming environments, featuring implementations of three approaches: a baseline method utilizing a pre-trained NER model, a disambiguation strategy based on graph embeddings, and an end-to-end neural architecture. Experiments conducted on two real-world datasets demonstrate that the embedding-based method achieves superior performance in certain scenarios, while the end-to-end model offers greater robustness.

This work presents a comprehensive calculation of one-loop oblique corrections for all MSSM Higgs doublets, which are expressed in terms of the masses and couplings of the complete set of scalar particles. The analysis covers the contributions of all fermions and gauge bosons, while the impact of scalar particles is treated separately.

We introduce a new challenge: synthesizing a 3D view of a dynamic scene from a single unstructured video clip. Unlike existing dynamic view synthesis methods, which rely on multiple calibrated videos, our approach operates on a single unstructured input. We propose a novel framework that simultaneously estimates 3D dynamic geometry and camera poses for novel viewpoints, leveraging a neural radiance field (NeRF) to model the scene. This work examines rough differential equations (RDEs) with a non-linear damping term, $x\mapsto a(x)x$, where the coefficient $a$ is not required to be Lipschitz continuous. We establish sufficient conditions on the coefficients to guarantee the existence of an $L^p$-bounded global solution for the scalar case, and further prove that the existence of a bounded solution in the Banach space $B_{\infty,\infty}^{\alpha}$ (with $\alpha>1/3$) implies the existence of a unique solution in the same space. These findings are derived by applying the contraction mapping principle to the integral form of the RDE, utilizing the specific properties of the exponential map associated with the logarithmic convexity of the coefficient $a$.
