This article series explores the application of functional programming within the orchestration and management of virtualized network resources. The initial installment examined the specific challenges and opportunities inherent in utilizing functional programming for this domain. This second installment examines the evolution of networking principles, emphasizing the design characteristics of modern networks and the critical role of abstraction in their management. Furthermore, it details how functional programming facilitates the management of these networks by leveraging type systems to ensure the reliability of management applications.

We investigate the toric code, a topological quantum error-correcting model, specifically regarding its two- and three-qubit gate operations. We demonstrate that the code's stabilizer generators can be expressed as sums of three Pauli matrices, which allows us to characterize the sets of gates that leave these generators invariant. Furthermore, we analyze the computational power of the toric code when combined with Clifford gates, showing that it can implement any two-qubit gate and three-qubit Toffoli gate. We also prove that the circuit depth required to realize these gates is optimal. Finally, we establish that the set of stabilizer generators is sufficient to generate all gates within the Clifford+T framework.

OPUS is a job control system designed for the Virtual Observatory (VO) that enables users to define tasks using VO data model standards, such as the VO Service Core (VOSC) and VO User Services (VUS). The system's primary goal is to offer an interoperable job control environment for the VO. This is achieved by defining a standard set of services that can be implemented in various ways by different VO components. Additionally, OPUS aims to function as a foundational element for VO components, including the Virtual Observatory Image Server (VOIS) and the Virtual Observatory Data Access System (VODAS).

This paper introduces a novel approach to teaching complex wireless networks by integrating digital game-based learning (DGBL) with 3D visualization. The proposed DGBL framework is designed to enhance student engagement, motivation, and self-efficacy, thereby improving learning outcomes. To achieve this, we developed a specialized 3D visualizer for complex wireless networks and constructed a corresponding DGBL environment. The system was tested with a cohort of 100 undergraduate students, and the findings indicate that this method significantly boosts both interest and self-efficacy, leading to superior learning results.

Ozone serves as a proxy for molecular oxygen in Earth's atmosphere, yet this relationship is not straightforward. This study examines the link between O₂ and O₃ concentrations across a broad range of planetary conditions, specifically focusing on the impact of varying stellar flux and atmospheric oxygen levels. We demonstrate that the oxygen photolysis rate is the primary driver of the O₂-O₃ relationship, with the ozone abundance rising as this rate decreases. Consequently, for planets orbiting cooler stars, the ozone-to-oxygen ratio can exceed that of Earth by several orders of magnitude. Furthermore, we identify a critical threshold in oxygen partial pressure below which the ozone signal becomes undetectable, regardless of the oxygen content. This suggests that the ozone signal may be entirely absent in Earth-analogs orbiting M dwarfs with oxygen partial pressures below 10⁻⁶ bar.

We investigate the transport characteristics of the three-dimensional (3D) Hofstadter model, which features a square lattice with perpendicular magnetic fields applied to its two top and bottom surfaces. Our findings indicate that the 3D Hofstadter model exhibits robust, nonequilibrium surface currents that endure against disorder and interactions. These currents are topologically protected by the bulk's nontrivial 3D Chern number and emerge on both the top and bottom boundaries of the system. We demonstrate that the bulk-boundary correspondence in this context is a manifestation of the bulk topology, which dictates the existence of these surface currents.

Although Neural Machine Translation (NMT) has achieved significant success in general-purpose language translation, its performance within specialized domains like medicine remains limited. This study evaluates the efficacy of domain-adapted multilingual NMT systems for medical applications. We examine two specific areas: (1) the degree to which medical text classification is influenced by domain adaptation, and (2) the extent to which such adaptation enhances medical machine translation. Our findings indicate that domain adaptation substantially improves translation quality for medical content, though its impact on text classification is minimal.

This study examines the generation of modified ion-acoustic (IA) solitary waves and shock waves within a plasma environment comprising non-thermally distributed electrons, positive dust particles, and a mixture of cold and warm ions. By applying the reductive perturbation technique, we derive a modified KdV equation to determine the conditions for solitary wave formation. The analysis indicates that the inclusion of positively charged dust and warm ions significantly alters the characteristics of both the modified KdV equation and the resulting solitons. Furthermore, we derive a modified Burgers equation to investigate the formation of shock waves. Our findings reveal that positively charged dust and non-thermal electron distributions substantially modify the shock formation criteria and shock properties. Additionally, we identify a critical ion-to-dust mass ratio threshold; when this ratio exceeds the critical value, the system supports both modified ion-acoustic solitons and shocks. Finally, we present numerical results to substantiate the theoretical analysis.

Dense retrieval has emerged as a leading technique for search engines, yet its application to low-resource languages remains limited. This paper introduces ContextAwareDocRep, an unsupervised pretraining method designed to enhance dense retrieval performance across multiple languages. Unlike standard sentence representations, ContextAwareDocRep incorporates contextual information from the surrounding document, thereby capturing inter-sentence relationships. We employ a masked language modeling (MLM) objective to train the model to predict masked tokens within sentences, using context-aware document representations as input. Experimental results demonstrate that ContextAwareDocRep significantly outperforms existing baselines in dense retrieval tasks across various language pairs. Additionally, we present a novel evaluation metric for passage retrieval that accounts for the specific characteristics of different languages.

Multimodal learning has gained significant traction in recent years, yet most existing methods fail to account for the inherent imbalance among different modalities. This imbalance arises from two primary factors: first, the disparity in the number of available samples across modalities, and second, the disparity in the information content they convey. To address these challenges, we introduce PMR, a straightforward yet effective technique designed to mitigate modality imbalance. PMR operates by generating samples for underrepresented modalities through a two-stage process: initially, it identifies prototypical instances within the target modality, and subsequently, it synthesizes additional samples by blending these prototypes with samples from overrepresented modalities. Empirical evaluations across various tasks, including image classification, object detection, and video action recognition, demonstrate that PMR consistently enhances performance. Notably, the method yields substantial gains in scenarios characterized by severe modality imbalance. Furthermore, the approach is computationally efficient, requiring no extra parameters and incurring negligible computational overhead. The accompanying code is accessible at https://github.com/Chenrui2000/PMR.

This study examines the transport dynamics of a relativistic gas featuring two-particle vector interactions, utilizing the classical Landau kinetic equation. We derive a set of relativistic kinetic equations for distribution functions and momenta, which are subsequently recast into a macroscopic hydrodynamic framework. The resulting equations of state and constitutive relations are expressed through the energy-momentum tensor and spin-antispin tensors. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these interaction models generate spin vorticity within the fluid. Finally, we analyze the behavior of such systems in both flat and curved spacetime environments.

This study introduces a new approach to spoken command recognition that leverages a tensor-train (TT) network. The method involves decomposing the input audio into a sequence of tensors, each representing a specific time step, and then processing these tensors through the TT network. The architecture of the TT network is designed to capture interdependencies between adjacent time steps. To enhance the model's ability to handle complex relationships, we integrate a hybrid architecture that combines the tensor-train network with a convolutional neural network (CNN). This hybrid model is trained using a dataset of 1,000 distinct spoken commands. The results demonstrate that the proposed CNN-TT hybrid model achieves superior performance compared to both the standalone tensor-train network and a standard CNN.

We introduce a technique for constructing quantum-jump paths corresponding to specific stochastic master equations (SMEs) derived from different representations of the underlying quantum trajectory theory. This approach is demonstrated through the analysis of a driven qubit subject to both dissipative decay and incoherent driving. Furthermore, we explore how these jump dynamics influence the outcomes of continuous quantum measurements.

This study investigates the impact of plasmonic aluminum nanoparticles with varying geometries on the optical absorption within thin-film silicon solar cells. The research analyzes the influence of particle shape, size, and interparticle distance on the resulting optical properties. The findings indicate that the absorption enhancement is most pronounced when the aluminum nanoparticles are arranged in a hexagonal lattice.

We introduce a logic designed to characterize $k$-variable PTIME on ordered structures, extending Datalog with a choice operator. This logic is a subset of Datalog$^{\rm{FO}}$, a known PTIME-complete framework for ordered structures that includes counting constructs. Our primary achievement involves a logic that avoids using these counting constructs. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the logic can be evaluated in polynomial time, even on unordered structures, provided the number of variables is fixed.

Lately, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks have become a leading approach for video recognition. Nevertheless, their high computational demands and memory usage make them difficult to deploy on energy-constrained edge devices. To address this, we introduce a novel algorithm and hardware co-design strategy that leverages Hierarchical Tucker (HTK) tensor decomposition to optimize LSTM networks for video recognition tasks. Our method involves three key components: first, a hierarchical Tucker decomposition of the LSTM's weight tensors; second, a hierarchical tensor-based quantization technique that reduces the bit-width of these weights and activations; and third, a specialized architecture featuring a Tucker-based LSTM layer and a Tucker-based Long Short-Term Memory cell. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves a 99.4% accuracy rate on the action recognition dataset UCF101, while cutting energy consumption by 98.4% and reducing memory footprint by 93.4%.

The MAVLink protocol serves as a standard communication interface for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) developed by ArduPilot and PX4, facilitating data exchange between the vehicle and ground control stations. However, its current design lacks essential security measures, leaving it susceptible to various cyberattacks. This paper introduces MAVSec, a security enhancement that secures MAVLink communications by implementing a lightweight authentication mechanism alongside encryption. The proposed solution is adaptable to diverse security requirements, ranging from low-power, resource-constrained devices to high-performance drones. Additionally, the authors have developed a comprehensive threat model and validated the system's effectiveness through rigorous testing on a quadcopter platform.

The Kollaps system enables the creation of decentralized, dynamic network topologies by allowing users to define and execute specific network scenarios. It operates by having participants run a lightweight client that communicates with others to synthesize a consistent view of the network. This approach is designed to be efficient, requiring minimal bandwidth and low computational overhead, while ensuring that the resulting network topology is both transparent and auditable.

This work outlines a straightforward, direct method for constructing the Newman-Penrose (NP) map, which translates a spacetime metric into an NP formalism. Our approach fundamentally relies on twistor techniques applied to flat space, specifically utilizing the known mapping between twistor functions and field strength tensors. By treating field strength tensors as gauge potentials, we demonstrate that this technique yields the NP formalism in a more streamlined manner compared to traditional methods.

This study introduces an innovative underground muon tomography technique designed to map the internal structures of large-scale objects. The proposed detector system utilizes a linear array of 120 plastic scintillator bars, each measuring 1 meter in length and 10 mm in width, which are read out via wavelength shifting paint and photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) at both extremities. The research outlines the detector's construction, operational principles, and the data processing algorithms required to extract the necessary information. The system is intended to be positioned within a tunnel beneath the Gran Sasso National Laboratory in Italy, situated 400 meters underground. The primary objective is to utilize this detector to image the internal architecture of the massive Adrona Tunnel, which extends 21.5 km in length and reaches a maximum depth of 1,100 meters below the surface.

This paper introduces a deterministic, linear-time-on-the-input parsing algorithm for Disjunctive Parsing Expression Grammars (PEGs), extending our previously proposed deterministic linear-time-on-the-input parsing algorithm for Ordered-Subsequence-Free Parsing Expression Grammars (OSF-PEGs). While PEGs and PEG GLL parsers are widely recognized for their utility, they suffer from exponential worst-case time complexity regarding the number of grammar rules. In contrast, the GLL parser for OSF-PEGs offers linear worst-case time complexity. This work extends that linear worst-case time complexity to PEG GLL parsers by incorporating disjunctions into the PEG grammar.

This study examines the vacuum Cherenkov radiation of ultra-high-energy particles within Lorentz-violating frameworks at finite temperatures. We demonstrate that thermal effects can substantially enhance the radiation rate, potentially leading to significant energy losses for ultra-high-energy cosmic rays. Furthermore, we analyze the energy loss mechanisms of ultra-high-energy neutrinos in the early universe, concluding that thermal corrections could have markedly influenced Big Bang Nucleosynthesis.

Although deep neural language models have achieved high accuracy in predicting naturalistic text, their internal representations remain opaque, making it difficult to interpret how these models derive their forecasts. To address this, we introduce a new method for tracking linguistic features throughout the prediction process of next tokens. This approach employs a set of specialized auxiliary models designed to monitor the evolution of specific linguistic properties as words are predicted sequentially. We validate this methodology using predictions from the BERT model on a corpus of English Wikipedia articles, demonstrating that it can effectively capture and explain the dynamic changes in linguistic features during generation.

We introduce a new approach to 3D object pose estimation that utilizes a straightforward yet effective strategy: generating synthetic views by rotating an object around its center. This technique, termed "accidental turntables," involves rendering a 3D model at a specific orientation and applying a random rotation to that view. We demonstrate that a neural network trained on these rotated pairs can accurately estimate 6DoF poses from a single image. This method is particularly advantageous for novel categories where 3D models exist but annotated data is absent. We validate our framework across three datasets—HDD-300, DTU, and TACO—covering both known and unknown categories. Our results indicate that the model achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods while requiring only a single input image.

We investigate charge transport in a hybrid superconductor-semiconductor nanowire system, where a magnetic field is applied perpendicular to the wire. This setup generates Andreev bound states (ABSs) at the interfaces between the superconductor and the wire. While these states are typically degenerate, our analysis reveals that they split into two distinct states with opposite spins when the magnetic field is oriented parallel to the nanowire. This spin splitting enables the control of crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) and subgap elastic co-tunneling mediated by ABSs (SACM). Specifically, the parallel magnetic field allows for the switching between the two spin states, which in turn modulates the CAR current. Additionally, the system exhibits a robust, gate-tunable, and highly efficient spin-to-charge conversion mechanism.

Particle acceleration driven by magnetic reconnection is a fundamental process in astrophysical plasmas. While the mechanism is well-established for electrons, its application to ions remains debated. This study investigates the acceleration of ions within the 2D Sweet-Parker layer of magnetic reconnection using a hybrid kinetic-fluid simulation. We introduce a pitch-angle scattering mechanism to account for the influence of small-scale turbulence on particle dynamics. Our results indicate that this scattering process significantly enhances ion energization, resulting in a power-law energy distribution with a spectral index of approximately 1.5. Furthermore, we observe that the total energy gain increases as the scattering rate rises.

This study examines the potential of the Higgs boson diphoton decay channel ($H\to\gamma\gamma$) and the associated production process $e^+e^-\to Zh$ for detecting new physics within the framework of the Two-Higgs-Doublet Model (2HDM). We demonstrate that, even with a limited integrated luminosity of 1 ab$^{-1}$, the combined analysis of these two processes can effectively constrain extended scalar sectors. Specifically, we find that the $H\to\gamma\gamma$ decay offers significant sensitivity to light CP-odd scalars, while the $e^+e^- \to Zh$ channel provides robust constraints on light CP-even scalars. Furthermore, we illustrate that the interplay between these two measurements enables the detection of light scalars with masses up to 10 GeV, achieving this sensitivity across a broad range of Higgs boson masses.

This paper provides formulas for the subdifferential of the joint numerical radius applied to $n$-tuples of bounded linear operators on a Hilbert space. Furthermore, we derive formulas for the corresponding gradients regarding the joint numerical radius for $n$ \*-tuples of bounded linear positive self operators on a Hilbert space. Finally, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions under which such an $n \*-tuples of bounded linear positive self operators results in a joint numerical radius that attains its minimum value.

Differential privacy (DP) is a rigorous mathematical framework designed to safeguard individual privacy within datasets. This paper introduces a novel DP application tailored for financial vision tasks, specifically leveraging the intersection of DP and vision for such purposes. We present a new methodology for estimating the privacy budget required by a vision model, utilizing the concept of "vision entropy" to achieve this. Our findings indicate that this approach is more precise than existing methods, particularly when applied to financial datasets. Additionally, we demonstrate that the proposed vision entropy metric can effectively determine the optimal level of noise for private vision models.

This study investigates the statistical characteristics of stochastic mappings between two measurable spaces, $X$ and $Y$, where $X$ is endowed with a measure $\mu$ and $Y$ with a measure $
u$. The analysis centers on the space $L^2(\mu)$ of square-integrable functions on $X$ and $L^2(
u)$ of square-integrable functions on $Y$. A stochastic mapping is defined as a random variable $f: \Omega 	o L^2(
u)$ that is square-integrable with respect to a probability measure $P$ on $\Omega$, satisfying the condition that its expected value of the squared $L^2(
u)$ norm equals one. The paper establishes a novel random distribution field (RDF) as a specific instance of such a stochastic mapping. Furthermore, it demonstrates that the space of all stochastic mappings between $L^2(
u)$ and $L^2(\mu)$ is isomorphic to the space of stochastic kernels from $L^2(
u)$ to $L^2(\mu)$. The work also examines the covariance structure of these mappings and introduces a covariance-based metric to quantify the distance between them. Finally, the paper outlines a method for constructing a stochastic mapping between $L^2(
u)$ and $L^2(\mu)$ given two RDFs, $f$ and $g$, and a specified covariance function $Cov(f,g)$.

This study examines the ignition of high-pressure (up to 10 bar) hydrogen-oxygen-helium mixtures using a defocused laser, with helium serving as a diluent. The results indicate that laser ignition efficiency in these conditions is governed by the interplay between the mixture's optical properties and the laser's intensity profile. Specifically, the laser intensity undergoes significant attenuation as it penetrates the mixture due to strong absorption by the hydrogen-oxygen-helium environment. This attenuation correlates with the mixture's optical depth, which is determined by the diluent's concentration and the laser's intensity profile. Consequently, the ignition kinetics of the mixture are driven by the competition between the laser intensity's attenuation and the chemical reaction rate.

This study introduces a new approach to semantic segmentation tailored for mobile and web environments, specifically addressing the need for compact, efficient models. The proposed method utilizes a dual-branch architecture: one branch focuses on global context while the other emphasizes local details. To enhance the boundary awareness of the network, we integrate a boundary-aware loss function and a post-processing module. The latter employs a dual-scale strategy to generate a refined segmentation map. Extensive experiments on the PASCAL VOC dataset demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art results with significantly reduced model complexity.

This study introduces a cooperative driver messenger system designed to aid lane changes by utilizing a vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication network. The system operates on the principle that a vehicle detects nearby units and alerts them when it intends to switch lanes, allowing neighboring units to subsequently inform the driver. The research details the system's architecture, including its communication protocol, and validates its performance through simulations. The results indicate that the system can effectively prevent collisions, provided that the necessary number of participating vehicles is present.

This study examines the motion of noninteracting weakly active particles within diverse geometrical configurations, specifically addressing how boundaries influence their dynamics. We demonstrate that the presence of boundaries can generate a non-zero mean-squared displacement (MSD) slope at short times, accompanied by a corresponding non-zero skewness in the probability distribution function (PDF) of displacements. Furthermore, we establish that the sign of the PDF skewness correlates with the sign of the MSD's initial linear slope. These findings are validated through numerical simulations of particles in one-dimensional confined spaces, two-dimensional planar domains, and three-dimensional spherical geometries.

This work introduces a modification to the average atom model by integrating Siegert states, which are unbound resonances occurring near the ionization threshold. These states arise from the temporary trapping of photoelectrons within the classical turning point of the outermost electron orbit. We demonstrate that including these Siegert states in atomic data calculations significantly refines the description of photoionization cross sections for highly charged ions, particularly under conditions where the photoenergy is close to the ionization limit.

This study presents an analysis of a solar flare observed by the Solar Dynamics Observatory's Imaging Telescope (IRIS) at a sub-second cadence. The observations reveal rapid, sub-second spectral variations in the Si IV 140.3 nm line, which are spatially localized to the flare's footpoints. The Si IV line profiles exhibit a broadening of approximately 100 km s$^{-1}$, with a 100 km s$^{-1}$ shift in the line center occurring within a 10-second window. The line center shift correlates with flare intensity, while the broadening increases with height above the solar surface. The QCD $\theta$-term, which is not restricted by any symmetry, introduces a CP violation that is experimentally constrained to be extremely small. This stringent limit has led to the proposal of the axion as a solution to the strong CP problem. However, the discovery of the axion's existence would provide the first experimental proof of the Peccei-Quinn mechanism, which is a $U(1)$ symmetry known to be a prerequisite for any theory that unifies all forces. Consequently, observing an axion would offer a direct pathway toward discovering supersymmetry and a theory of Grand Unification.

Plagiarism detection in source code is a complex issue that has attracted significant attention from both academic and industrial sectors. While numerous detection methods have been developed, the primary objective of this research is to create a source code anti-plagiarism system. This system operates by identifying the source of the copy, thereby discouraging future plagiarism and mitigating its negative impacts. To achieve this, the study introduces a Routing Approach that segments code into distinct blocks, which are subsequently processed by a machine learning classifier to determine if any block resembles content from another file. This paper outlines the implementation of this Routing Approach using C#.

This paper establishes the absolute convergence of automorphic Dirichlet series in a half-plane, where the boundary corresponds to a specific spectral threshold. This boundary condition aligns perfectly with cases known to exhibit absolute convergence. Our approach utilizes the Rankin-Selberg integral, enhanced by a novel technique for estimating integrals over nilmanifolds.

This paper investigates the properties of $(k,\epsilon)$-metric approximate subgroups within metric groups, extending concepts from integer-based analogues. Our primary findings include a classification of these approximate subgroups via model sets, alongside an examination of model sets in metric contexts. Additionally, we establish a metric version of the approximate subgroup lemma and derive upper bounds for their covering numbers.

Log-concave density estimation is a nonparametric statistical method that yields consistent estimators with a convergence rate comparable to parametric approaches. While recent advances have introduced new algorithms for univariate and bivariate cases, this paper presents a framework for estimating densities in any dimension $d \geq 1$. We demonstrate that the optimization problem underlying log-concave density estimation can be reformulated as a convex quadratic program with linear constraints, enabling the use of efficient numerical solvers. Our approach is validated through experiments on both simulated and real datasets, and we further address the estimation of the support set for log-concave densities.

This study introduces an entropic sampling approach based on Wang-Landau algorithms, designed to investigate static granular systems at fixed volume and particle number. By employing a microstate representation where particles are positioned on arches, the method utilizes an efficient algorithm to calculate the local change in contact forces resulting from particle displacements. This facilitates the exploration of the system's configuration space and the estimation of the entropic landscape. The approach is applied to two-dimensional repulsive granular packings, where the resulting entropic microstate distribution is compared against canonical ensemble simulations. Furthermore, the study examines the system's equation of state and its dependence on the participation ratio.

This paper investigates a two-player game played on a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, where the Explorer-Director duo aims to visit every node. The Explorer moves one step per turn and must be guided by the Director, who possesses full knowledge of the graph's structure. The Director must specify the next available neighbor of the Explorer's position at each turn. The central problem is determining the minimum number of bits the Director needs to send to guarantee a complete traversal of all vertices. This quantity is defined as the *directorial dimension* of $G$. We establish that for any graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, this dimension is bounded above by $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil + 1$. Furthermore, we prove that for any $\epsilon > 0$, there exist graphs requiring a dimension of at least $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil - \epsilon$. Finally, we analyze the properties of graphs that achieve a constant directorial dimension.

We propose a new methodology for establishing energy conservation in incompressible Euler flows, applicable to weak solutions that possess bounded energy and a vorticity which is energy bounded. This approach is particularly effective for proving energy conservation in 2D and 3D settings where vorticities are bounded in the $L^p$ space with $p>3$.

VIRUP is a virtual reality platform designed to facilitate the visualization and analysis of astronomical data. It offers a fully immersive experience, allowing users to navigate seamlessly between 2D and 3D representations of the cosmos. The system supports the visualization of diverse data types, including galaxy catalogs, simulations, and various 3D structures. The platform is built on a modular architecture, where each component is designed to be easily replaceable, ensuring that new data sources or visualization techniques can be integrated without disrupting the entire system. The article details the platform's architecture, implementation, and key features, while also presenting a use case involving the interactive exploration of the Millennium simulation.

The Data Bricks Space Mission is a data literacy program designed for children aged 6 to 12, utilizing a narrative-driven approach where a space mission provides the context for learning. This scenario-based method engages young learners by framing abstract data concepts within a compelling story. The program is structured into three sequential stages: a data collection phase, a data processing phase, and a data visualization phase. During collection, participants gather data through a virtual mission control interface. Next, in the processing stage, they analyze this information using a simplified version of a spreadsheet. Finally, in the visualization phase, they create a 3D physical model of a solar system to display their findings. This innovative visualization technique transforms intangible data into tangible insights, enabling children to grasp complex concepts through direct physical interaction.

Software-Defined Networking (SDN) has emerged as a dominant paradigm in network management, offering enhanced programmability and flexibility. However, the extensive configuration space within SDN-driven data planes creates significant challenges for network operators. To address this, we introduce a data-path identification algorithm designed to extract operational data paths from large-scale, complex SDN-driven environments. Our approach leverages the inherent flow table hierarchy in SDN controllers to efficiently isolate active paths. We have implemented this algorithm on a real-world SDN testbed and evaluated its performance against existing methods. The results demonstrate that our algorithm achieves superior efficiency in identifying operational data paths within large-scale SDN-driven networks.

Disentangled representation learning aims to acquire representations that isolate specific, independent factors of variation. While prior research has largely focused on learning these representations from scratch, this paper introduces a novel approach that leverages pre-existing knowledge to facilitate the acquisition of weakly disentangled representations. Specifically, we utilize relational data concerning the factors of variation to guide the learning process. Our proposed method, Disentangled Representation Learning with External Knowledge (DREK), integrates this external knowledge as a regularizer to encourage the acquisition of such representations. We validate DREK across two distinct domains: weakly supervised clustering and weakly supervised representation learning. Experimental results demonstrate that DREK consistently outperforms baseline methods in both tasks.

This study investigates the hydrodynamic interaction between tandem oscillating foils, specifically examining how the wake of a leading foil influences the performance of a trailing one. The research utilizes a two-dimensional numerical model to simulate the flow dynamics and structural vibrations of two heaving foils, with the objective of maximizing the energy harvested by both elements. The analysis focuses on the relationship between the spacing between foils and the peak power output, alongside the influence of the angle of attack on the resulting flow structures. Findings indicate that the most efficient configuration involves a specific gap distance and an optimal negative angle of attack, which facilitates the generation of a leading-edge vortex. This phenomenon promotes a phase shift in the vortex shedding of the second foil, thereby enhancing energy extraction. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the leading vortex effectively suppresses the formation of a trailing vortex, resulting in a flow pattern characterized by two distinct vortex pairs.

We introduce a new methodology for Bayesian inference of real-time dynamics in quantum field theories, utilizing lattice QCD as a proof of concept. This approach employs a Bayesian framework to infer real-time evolution from Euclidean lattice data, specifically targeting the two-point correlation function of the pion. By integrating Euclidean and real-time observables within a single Bayesian analysis, we demonstrate that this method is capable of delivering reliable real-time results.

This approach involves modulating the gate voltage of the dot to trigger electron tunneling events, followed by detecting the resulting gate-induced shift in the island's charge state. De novo drug discovery is a critical and difficult endeavor. While traditional methods rely on trial-and-error, they are often inefficient and costly. Consequently, there is a growing demand for computational tools that can accelerate this process. In this study, we introduce a generative model designed to create drug molecules with specific target affinities. Our approach employs a variational autoencoder (VAE) to capture the latent space of molecular structures, utilizing a molecular graph energy function to ensure the selected molecules are biologically viable. We demonstrate the model's effectiveness by training it to generate molecules that bind to the HCV NS3/4A protease. Furthermore, we validate that the proposed model can produce molecules with target-specific properties.

The Machine for Introducing Geometry (MaG) is a recent formal system that offers a novel way to model computation using a graph rewriting framework. This approach is inspired by the Geometry of Interaction (GoI) paradigm, which interprets linear logic as an algebra of interaction. MaG is designed to be both expressive and efficient, capable of simulating the original Geometry of Interaction (GoI) while also handling a broader range of token-based computations. In this paper, we present a formal definition of the MaG rewriting rules and provide a proof of its confluence.

We present proper motion measurements for the outer regions of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) derived from the VST Mega-Mag project. Utilizing 1.5 years of data from the VST's MegaCam instrument, we analyzed 1.5 million stars with a limiting magnitude of $g=20$ to achieve a median proper motion of $-0.06 \pm 0.01$ mas/yr in right ascension and $-0.02 \pm 0.01$ mas/yr in declination. These values align with the previously established VMC survey results for the inner LMC. The study also examines the proper motion of the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) and its surrounding areas, revealing a median motion of $-0.03 \pm 0.01$ mas/yr in right ascension and $-0.03 \pm 0.01$ mas/yr in declination. These findings are consistent with prior SMC motion studies. Furthermore, we investigate the influence of the SMC on the LMC's kinematics, noting that the SMC's proper motion is approximately 0.02 mas/yr closer to the LMC than the LMC is to the SMC. Consequently, the LMC is moving away from the SMC.

Electricity theft detection within Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) networks is critical for utilities to safeguard their revenue. While numerous machine learning approaches have been developed for this purpose, most depend on fixed hyper-parameters that are often ill-suited to specific data characteristics. This study introduces a novel hyper-parameter tuning strategy designed to enhance the performance of deep recurrent neural networks for theft detection. The method employs a multi-objective optimization framework that utilizes a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) to identify an optimal set of hyper-parameters. This process is supported by a custom-designed fitness function that balances the trade-off between detection accuracy and computational cost. The efficacy of this approach is validated using real-world smart meter data from an actual AMI system.

This work introduces a novel inductive methodology for analyzing the surface topology of tight surface graphs (TSGs). A TSG is defined as a combinatorial embedding of a trivalent planar graph on a closed surface that attains the minimum possible vertex count for that genus. We establish a constructive proof of existence for these minimal configurations and demonstrate that the resulting structures are intrinsically linked to the canonical triangulations of the surface.

This study reports the first simultaneous measurement of the lifetimes for the $\Omega^{0}_{c}$ and $\Xi^{0}_{c}$ baryons, utilizing the $\Omega^{0}_{c} \to \Lambda^{0} K^{-}\pi^{+}$ and $\Xi^{0}_{c} \to \Lambda^{0} \pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ decay channels. Data were collected by the LHCb detector at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 3.0 fb$^{-1}$. The derived lifetimes are $\tau(\Omega^{0}_{c}) = 2.01 \pm 0.01 \pm 0.02$ ps and $\tau(\Xi^{0}_{c}) = 1.22 \pm 0.01 \pm 0.02$ ps, where the first uncertainties are statistical and the second are systematic.

This study introduces a novel subspace clustering framework designed for unsupervised hyperspectral image classification. By leveraging the inherent low-rank structure of the data, the proposed method constructs a similarity matrix that is subsequently converted into a subspace affinity matrix. This transformation is achieved through a newly developed subspace clustering algorithm that incorporates a similarity constraint. This constraint ensures that the resulting affinity matrix remains non-negative and symmetric, thereby enhancing clustering accuracy. Furthermore, the algorithm employs a fast and efficient optimization strategy to solve the resulting non-convex problem. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

The Arctic sea ice surface is covered by a layer of snow, which significantly influences the ice's albedo and mechanical properties. However, current models of snow accumulation and redistribution on sea ice are inadequate, largely due to a lack of understanding regarding the complex topography that develops. This study introduces a simplified model for snow dune formation on ice, driven by the interplay between wind and the underlying roughness. The model demonstrates that dune formation is a self-organizing process that generates a self-similar topography characterized by a power-law distribution of dune sizes. This distribution is defined by a single scaling parameter, which is determined by the wind speed, ice roughness, and the density of the snow layer. The model successfully reproduces the observed dune sizes found on Arctic sea ice. Furthermore, it predicts a "snow dune" regime where the snow layer is discontinuous, featuring deep troughs that remain ice-exposed. This regime aligns with recent observations of dune formation on Arctic sea ice and offers a more realistic representation of snow-covered ice surfaces than previous models.

We introduce a selective quantum effect known as the Zeno phenomenon, which inhibits the conversion of ultracold atoms into molecules through selective blocking of the atomic scattering process. This is accomplished by utilizing a time-oscillating magnetic field that induces Rabi oscillations between two molecular states, while employing a tailored time-dependent amplitude to dynamically suppress the scattering interaction. This approach offers a pathway to selectively manage ultracold atom-molecule reactions, potentially enabling the creation of specific ultracold molecules with tailored properties.

This study introduces a generalized Ito-Langevin framework tailored for nonextensive statistical mechanics, where the associated probability distribution is characterized by Tsallis's q-entropy. We demonstrate that this formalism adheres to the standard Ito-Langeville equations when $q$ equals 1, and to the Gaussian case when $q$ equals 2. Furthermore, we examine the implications of this generalized approach for the statistical attributes of Brownian motion.

This study examines the optical excitation of a nodal-line semimetal, specifically focusing on the generation of higher-order topological states. By applying circularly polarized light within the infrared range, we induce a bandgap transition that transforms the system into an insulator featuring Weyl nodes. These nodes function as sources of a nontrivial Berry curvature, thereby establishing a quantized multipole moment. The resulting topological insulator exhibits a corner state characterized by a quantized second-order topological invariant. Notably, the Weyl node count is sensitive to light intensity, while the topological invariant remains robust against light-induced disorder. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Weyl node count can be modulated by adjusting the light's frequency.

This paper introduces Marvel DC, a distributed computing protocol designed to ensure data privacy and computational integrity. Leveraging blockchain technology, Marvel DC enables participants to securely execute private computations on confidential data without revealing the underlying information. The protocol employs a distributed, decentralized architecture that allows nodes to perform computations on encrypted data while maintaining strict control over their access. Furthermore, it implements an incentive-compatible mechanism to prevent malicious behavior and ensure fair participation. The authors provide a comprehensive analysis of Marvel DC's security properties, including privacy, correctness, and robustness against various attacks. The paper also presents a detailed performance evaluation of Marvel DC, demonstrating its efficiency and scalability in real-world scenarios. Finally, the authors outline several potential future research directions aimed at further enhancing the protocol's functionality and applicability.

Point cloud compression (PCC) is a crucial technology for the efficient transmission of 3D data, a field that has seen significant advancements recently. Nevertheless, existing PCC standards, such as MPEG-DAS, still face limitations regarding the fidelity of reconstructed 3D models. To address this, we introduce a reduced reference perceptual quality model designed to evaluate the quality of compressed point clouds. This model operates on two primary principles: first, it assesses point cloud quality by analyzing the distribution of point density; second, it incorporates the concept of human visual attention to quantify visual quality. Leveraging this model, we developed a rate control algorithm for PCC, which dynamically adjusts compression parameters to balance visual quality against available bandwidth. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed approach achieves superior performance compared to current state-of-the-art PCC standards.

This study employs the dual holographic framework to investigate the QCD phase diagram. By utilizing the Sakai-Sugimoto model, we examine the behavior of thermal vector mesons and chiral symmetry restoration. Our analysis indicates that the transition occurs as a crossover, with the transition temperature ($T_c$) approximately at 200 MeV, aligning well with lattice QCD results. Furthermore, we employ the improved Sakai-Sugimoto model to explore finite-density QCD. Our findings reveal a first-order phase transition at high densities, which transforms into a crossover at lower densities, a scenario consistent with standard QCD expectations.

Deep learning has demonstrated significant potential for medical image analysis, particularly in detecting knee abnormalities. However, the scarcity of labeled data and the high cost of acquiring these labels remain significant obstacles. To address this, we introduce a novel Slice-Based Self-Supervised Learning (SB-SSL) framework designed to generate robust representations from individual MRI slices. This framework employs a self-supervised contrastive learning strategy that utilizes a masked slice reconstruction task to produce positive and negative samples. Furthermore, we incorporate a slice-level augmentation technique to enhance the diversity of these samples. Experimental results indicate that the proposed SB-SSL framework effectively learns high-quality features from slices, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the OAI dataset for the task of abnormality classification.

Font generation has gained significant attention in recent years, particularly for its ability to create new typography from minimal user input. While current methods typically rely on a small set of character examples to synthesize a full font, they often fail to capture fine-grained local styles, resulting in generated text that lacks the distinct nuances of the original characters. To address this, we introduce a new approach that utilizes glyph strokes as localized style units. By training on a small collection of glyphs, our method learns to synthesize entire fonts by assembling these localized styles. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments, showing that it successfully captures intricate details and produces high-quality fonts.

We investigate the interaction between thermal equilibrium and chiral torsion within relativistic hydrodynamics. Our analysis reveals that, unlike the standard chiral vortical effect, the chiral torsion effect is not driven by rotation. Instead, it arises from the interaction between chiral chemical potential and chiral torsion, with its magnitude scaling linearly with this chiral chemical potential.

Adaptive streaming delivers a high-quality viewing experience by dynamically adjusting video quality in response to fluctuating network conditions. However, achieving optimal quality remains difficult because of the significant variability in users' network environments and the diversity of their personal preferences. To address this, we introduce a novel, user-centric framework for adaptive streaming that simultaneously targets Quality of Experience (QoE) enhancement and preference personalization. This approach employs a digital twin to model the intricate relationship between network conditions and user preferences, thereby enabling the prediction of the most suitable quality level for each user. Furthermore, we have developed a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithm that leverages this digital twin to learn an optimal quality selection strategy. Experimental results indicate that the proposed DRL method outperforms existing state-of-the-art solutions in terms of both QoE and the alignment with user preferences.

This paper investigates the well-posedness of solutions to the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLEq) subject to white noise in the dispersion operator, a scenario modeling optical pulse propagation in disordered media. We demonstrate that the associated Cauchy problem remains well-posed for any realization of this stochastic operator. Furthermore, we establish the stability of the stochastic flow derived from the equation.

This study examines the challenge of delivering data packets within a specific deadline across multiple parallel wireless channels. We introduce a scheduling and coding framework that ensures reliable transmission with minimal latency. The system employs joint coding and scheduling, where packets are grouped into sets transmitted over parallel links using erasure codes. Each set is designed to guarantee at least one successful delivery per packet before the deadline. The packets within a set are partitioned into two categories: those transmitted over a single link and those over multiple links. The single-link transmission utilizes a Reed-Solomon code, while the multi-link transmission employs a Reed-Muller code. The allocation of packets to these categories is determined by a greedy algorithm that maximizes the number of successfully delivered packets. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that this approach achieves the maximum number of delivered packets for any given deadline. Furthermore, we propose a method to minimize the number of required packets for a fixed deadline, proving that our algorithm outperforms existing schemes.

The supernova remnant Sgr A East is located in the Galactic center, situated approximately 10 parsecs from the supermassive black hole Sgr A*. Theoretical models suggest that the explosion occurred near the black hole, leading to the accretion of a significant portion of the ejecta. This study examines the consequences of such a scenario on the Galactic center's environment. We find that the shock wave from the supernova would have traversed the central region, potentially triggering a new round of star formation. Furthermore, the explosion could have disrupted the central molecular zone and the Sgr A* accretion disk, while the resulting hot gas would have formed a low-density cavity around the black hole. The X-ray emission from Sgr A* is likely dominated by the accretion of supernova ejecta, which would be heated by shocks generated as the ejecta collide with the cavity walls. Theoretical calculations indicate that the ejecta would be confined within the cavity for roughly 100,000 years. Consequently, the current accretion rate onto SGR A* is estimated to be around 10^-3 solar masses per year.

Lepton flavor universality (LFU) is a fundamental tenet of the Standard Model, asserting that the weak interaction treats leptons of the same generation identially. However, recent experimental findings in B meson decays have hinted at potential violations of LFU, prompting significant interest in investigating these anomalies and their possible implications for physics beyond the Standard Model. This review examines the current status of these results, explores theoretical frameworks capable of explaining them, and analyzes the broader theoretical and experimental consequences of such deviations.

This paper details our team's approach to the DISRPT2021 shared task, which focuses on discourse segmentation, classification, and connective detection. We present a novel, modular system designed to handle all three subtasks. Our architecture leverages a pre-trained language model alongside a dedicated task-specific classifier for each component. Furthermore, we introduce a discourse tree bank for the DISRPT2021 English corpus and conduct an extensive analysis of the system's performance across various tasks.

The sixth generation (6G) of wireless communication is poised to deliver unprecedented capabilities, including ultra-high data rates, extensive coverage, and massive device connectivity. However, the growing demand for these services necessitates a shift from traditional, siloed infrastructure models to a collaborative, shared approach. This paper introduces a blockchain-enabled framework designed to facilitate secure and transparent sharing of infrastructure resources among diverse stakeholders. By leveraging distributed ledgers, the system ensures accountability and trust, enabling entities to monetize idle assets while accessing shared capacity. The study outlines the architecture of this sharing model, details the underlying consensus mechanisms, and demonstrates the framework's viability through a simulation of a 5G network.

The Okubo-Weiss criterion serves as a valuable tool for analyzing the evolution of vorticity in two-dimensional flows, specifically for identifying regions of potential Lagrangian coherent structures. This study examines the Okubo-Weiss criterion within the context of two-dimensional hydrodynamic and magnetohydrodynamic systems. We demonstrate that the criterion can be expressed as a weighted sum of the relative stretching and squeezing terms, where the weights are defined by the kinetic energy density and the magnetic field intensity. Furthermore, we establish that the Okubo-Weiss equation can be formulated as a transport equation for the relative stretching and squeezing terms, augmented by a source term. This derived form allows for a detailed examination of the mechanisms driving the evolution of the Okubo-Weiss quantity.

This study examines the thermodynamics of Lee-Wick (LW) fields within the cosmological evolution of the early universe. We demonstrate that the inclusion of a massive LW field in the cosmic background can trigger a phase transition from a non-relativistic to a relativistic regime, provided the LW field's mass is sufficiently low. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of LW fields on the cosmic expansion rate and the critical temperature associated with the electroweak phase transition. Our findings indicate that the presence of a light LW field can elevate this threshold, potentially transforming a weakly first-order process into a strongly first-order phase transition.

Image style transfer (ST) is a deep learning technique that applies the stylistic attributes of a source image to a content image. While recent advances in ST have yielded impressive results, they often struggle with artifacts and fail to capture the fine details of the source imagery. To address these limitations, we introduce a novel Transformer-based approach for Image Style Transfer (ST$^2$). This method utilizes a Transformer encoder-decoder architecture to effectively model long-range dependencies, thereby preserving intricate details. Furthermore, we incorporate a specialized attention module designed to capture both local and global stylistic features. Our experiments demonstrate that ST$^2$ achieves superior visual quality compared to existing ST methods.

Thermodynamic length, defined as the square root of the integrated squared difference between normalized traces of the rate of change of the system's Hamiltonian and the system's average energy, has been shown to equal twice the minimal frictional energy loss in isothermal protocols. This metric offers a concise characterization of the energetic cost of state transformations, independent of the specific path taken. This study experimentally demonstrates that protocols designed to minimize thermodynamic length achieve the optimal dissipation rate, even when executed at speeds significantly higher than the quasi-static limit. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this principle holds true for both isothermal and non-isothermal processes. These findings provide a practical framework for designing energy-efficient thermodynamic operations, particularly for implementing Landauer erasure.

This study examines the stability of inhomogeneous fluids subjected to acoustic fields, a phenomenon known as acoustically induced cavitation. The governing equations are the linearized Navier-Stokes equations, which are solved using a spectral method. The analysis reveals that the linear instability mechanism is driven by the interaction between the acoustic field and the density gradient. This process is characterized by a specific critical wavenumber, which is determined by the density gradient and the acoustic field's wavelength. The paper concludes that this mechanism is responsible for the formation of cavities in the fluid.

This study investigates the analytic properties of the powers of weighted shifts defined on generalized directed semi-trees. We demonstrate that the spectral radius of such an operator $T$ is characterized by $\|T^n\|^{1/n} = \sup_{v} |T^n v|/\|v^n\|$, which further simplifies to $\|Tv\|^{1/d(v)}$, where $d(v)$ represents the multiplicity of the vertex $v$. Furthermore, we establish that the operator $T$ is cyclic precisely when $T$ is isometric or when the shifts are located on a linear, one-dimensional directed semi-tree. Additionally, we show that $T$ is hypercontractive if and only if $T$ is unitarily equivalent to a unilateral weighted shift on the standard directed tree. Finally, we derive the hypercontractive condition for $T$ when it is considered as an operator on a weighted directed tree.

This study examines the production of radioactive nuclei and electron-positron pairs resulting from the interaction of a high-Z target with a gamma-ray flash produced by an ultra-intense laser operating in the $\lambda^3$ regime. The analysis incorporates the effects of the Coulomb field from the nucleus, the laser's electromagnetic field, and the resulting secondary photon field. We demonstrate that the Coulomb field significantly enhances the Compton scattering cross-section, thereby increasing the yield of secondary gamma-rays and the subsequent pair production rate. Furthermore, we evaluate the impact of these fields on the photofission cross-section and the resulting radioactive nuclei production. Our findings indicate that the Coulomb field substantially boosts the photofission cross-section, leading to a marked rise in radioactive nuclei generation. Additionally, we analyze the influence of the laser-generated electromagnetic field on both Compton scattering and pair production, concluding that the overall yield of secondary gamma-rays and pair production rises as laser intensity increases.

Event detection involves identifying the onset of specific occurrences within a continuous data stream. This paper introduces a novel approach to event detection that leverages Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) to capture event patterns. The method employs a custom-designed graph structure to model the temporal dependencies between data points. To address the challenge of limited event data, we integrate a diversity gate into the GCN framework. This gate utilizes a lightweight neural network to learn event patterns from the majority class (normal data) and applies them to detect anomalies. Furthermore, we incorporate a syntactic scoring mechanism to evaluate the relevance of input data points to the event being detected. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques across various datasets.

This study establishes geometric ergodicity for Gibbs samplers within a Bayesian error-in-variable regression framework. By employing a Markov chain approach, we prove that under mild conditions, the Markov chain's $\beta$-mixing property holds, which consequently implies the ergodicity of the Gibbs sampler. The proposed method is applied to a clinical trial dataset to evaluate the regression relationship between systolic and diastolic blood pressure.

This study introduces a new method for designing robust optimal control sequences in quantum sensing within a framework that accounts for both system evolution and interactions. The approach utilizes a two-step procedure: first, a multi-qubit interaction is modeled as a distinct qubit, and second, an optimal control sequence is derived for the effective reduced dynamics of this entity. The authors demonstrate that this strategy yields high-fidelity, robust control sequences for various sensing applications, including Ramsey interferometry and dynamical decoupling, while effectively managing interactions among multiple qubits. Furthermore, the method is validated through numerical simulations of a three-qubit system subjected to stochastic noise. The results indicate that this technique offers a straightforward and effective pathway for managing multi-qubit interactions in quantum sensing protocols.

This paper introduces a numerical approach to nonlinear dynamical systems subject to random noise, utilizing the Krylov subspace. The method employs a Gaussian noise model and uses the Karhunen-Loève expansion to represent the random noise. The resulting nonlinear system is then transformed into a higher-dimensional linear system with random noise, which is further projected into a lower-dimensional deterministic linear system. The method is applied to a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with random noise, demonstrating that the approach effectively captures the random noise's influence on the solution.

This study examines wave propagation within scattering media featuring nonlinear absorption, utilizing the radiative transfer equation (RTE) and the diffusion approximation of the RTE (DARTE). The research focuses on a plane wave entering a semi-infinite medium, with the goal of determining the corresponding source term for the 1D-RTE and its DARTE variant. To achieve this, the incoming plane wave is modeled as a Dirac delta function, and the solution is derived using the method of characteristics. The paper subsequently analyzes the behavior of the 1D-RTE and its corresponding approximations under two distinct scenarios: one where the incoming wave is a high-intensity pulse and the other where it is low-intensity.

Reinforcement learning (RL) has recently achieved significant breakthroughs across various domains, including robotics, gaming, and healthcare. Nevertheless, the deployment of these systems in critical sectors remains limited due to the "black-box" nature of their decision-making processes, which hinders human trust. To address this, researchers have developed explainable reinforcement learning (XRL) to enhance model transparency. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of XRL, beginning with a review of the fundamental challenges associated with applying RL in high-stakes environments. We then introduce the concept of explainable RL, detailing its primary methodologies and categorizing them into model-based and model-free approaches. Furthermore, the discussion covers the evaluation metrics used to assess these methods and explores the emerging field of safe XRL. Finally, the paper concludes by identifying current limitations and suggesting promising future research directions within XRL.

This work examines one-variable logics grounded in algebraic semantics, specifically those utilizing a variety of finite depth within the framework of linear lattices. We establish that these logics are decidable and possess the finite model property, with the added benefit of admitting axiomatizations based on finite sets of formulas. Furthermore, we demonstrate that certain such logics function as substructures of the two-element Boolean logic expanded with a specific constant and lattice disjunction.
We establish the Wiener chaos decomposition for the signature of Gaussian processes featuring stationary increments, specifically covering both integer and fractional orders.

Millimeter-wave (mmWave) cellular networks are anticipated to be pivotal for next-generation wireless systems, yet their performance is heavily contingent on the accuracy of the localization process. This study introduces a statistical framework to characterize the performance of the maximum likelihood (ML) localization estimator within a mmWave cellular environment. Specifically, we derive the asymptotic distribution of the ML estimator, which serves as a critical tool for assessing its accuracy. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this distributional model is robust across diverse scenarios, including varying densities of base stations, different channel models, and distinct configurations of the target location.

We examine a system comprising $N$ bosons confined to a volume $V$ and subject to a short-range repulsive interaction. The inter-particle potential is defined as $V_\lambda(r) = \lambda^2 V(r\lambda)$, where $V$ is a non-negative, integrable function with a finite second moment. The coupling constant $\lambda$ is determined by the thermodynamic condition $\lambda^3 = n^{-1}$. Assuming the system resides at a temperature $T$ exceeding the critical value $T_c$, we demonstrate that in the limit as $N \to \infty$, the fraction of particles occupying the ground state approaches $1 - T/T_c$.

Image inpainting involves reconstructing missing image regions by leveraging contextual information from surrounding areas. Although recent deep learning approaches have demonstrated significant potential for high-resolution image restoration, they often struggle with the computational demands of processing large images. To address this, we introduce a two-stage deep learning framework designed to enhance inpainting performance on high-resolution inputs. The initial stage utilizes a patch-based strategy to generate preliminary inpaintings for image segments, while the subsequent stage employs a global context network to refine these results by integrating patch-wise inpaintings with the original image's global context. Experimental results indicate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art inpainting techniques on both quantitative and qualitative benchmarks.

This study examines stochastic bandit problems characterized by an underlying latent structure, where the reward function is defined as the sum of a latent mean and a thresholded version of the latent function. The focus is on the specific scenario where the latent function is a step function. The primary objective is to derive regret bounds that are both tight and depend on the specific latent function. To address this, the authors introduce a novel metric termed "problem dependent view of structured bandits," which is a problem-specific generalization of the standard concept of effective horizon. The paper further demonstrates that the expected regret of the proposed algorithm is upper-bounded by a term involving the problem-dependent effective horizon and a problem-specific constant. Additionally, the study proves that the proposed algorithm achieves a constant regret in cases where the latent function is a step function.

This paper presents an algorithmic approach to compressing the proofs of the main theorem from the previously published work [1]. The authors of that earlier study claimed the existence of proofs within PSPACE-complete NP instances that have a polynomial in length, but lacked a concrete construction. In contrast, our paper provides a specific polynomial-time algorithm to generate these proofs.

This paper investigates the behavior of the $H^\alpha$-flow for hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$. We establish that the flow maintains the convexity of the mean curvature over time. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the flow can be extended indefinitely for the case $\alpha > 1$, provided the initial hypersurface is complete, convex, and possesses finite total curvature.

We establish sum rules governing vortex-pair fluctuations within a Coulomb-gas framework for two-dimensional superfluids. Derived from the first moment of the pair-pair correlation function, these relations hold regardless of short-range interaction specifics. By applying our findings to the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition, we determine the effective temperature-dependent vortex charge and line tension. Furthermore, we contrast our results with recent numerical simulations of a 2D XY model, noting that while the scaling of line tension aligns with the predictions, the overall magnitude differs.

As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into daily life, it is crucial to understand how the public perceives it. This study examines public knowledge, attitudes, and concerns regarding AI across eight nations. We conducted a representative survey of 1,000 participants in each country to assess their familiarity with AI, their attitudes toward its impact on employment and privacy, and their worries about AI's future. The findings reveal that while AI awareness is high in the surveyed nations, the public tends to view AI positively. Furthermore, the data indicates that the public's perception of AI is closely tied to their existing experience with technology.

The suppressed weak decay $\Xi_c^0\to \pi^-\Lambda_c^+$ has been observed for the first time with a measured branching fraction of $(1.0\pm0.3\pm0.2)\times10^{-3}$. This result is derived from an analysis of $pp$ collision data with a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s}=7$ TeV and an integrated luminosity of $3.0\pm0.08$ fb$^{-1}$ collected by the LHCb detector.

Based on these findings, we also provide convergence criteria for the products of the iterative sequences $x_{n+1}=T x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S x_{n}$, $x_{n+1}=T S x_{n} S

Actor-Critic (AC) reinforcement learning has proven highly effective for solving complex tasks, yet it remains susceptible to overfitting and local optima, particularly in high-dimensional spaces. This paper introduces a novel AC framework that integrates Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) to mitigate these challenges. By employing HMC to sample from the critic's parameter distribution, the method updates the actor's parameters using a gradient estimator derived from AC loss. We provide a theoretical analysis of the proposed algorithm and validate its performance through experiments on the Cartpole and LunarLander environments.

We investigate the Dicke model, which describes a system of interacting bosonic modes and spins, within a triangular lattice configuration. This setup exhibits a unique chiral quantum phase characterized by the spontaneous breaking of parity and time-reversal symmetries. We demonstrate that tricriticality occurs at the boundaries of this phase, which can be precisely mapped using the model's underlying discrete symmetries.

Although transfer learning has proven highly effective for single-agent reinforcement learning, its application to multi-agent settings remains largely unexplored. This paper introduces a novel cooperative multi-agent transfer learning framework that leverages knowledge from a source domain to accelerate policy learning in a target domain. We propose a level-adaptive credit assignment mechanism designed to dynamically adjust the degree of transfer based on the performance gap between source and target policies. Additionally, we develop a new action-state representation that unifies the source and target domains, thereby enhancing the transferability of policies. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing baselines across various cooperative multi-agent tasks.

Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has recently achieved significant success in robotic applications, yet the absence of realistic simulation environments tailored for multi-fingered manipulation and multi-agent navigation has hindered its practical deployment. To address this, we introduce a novel, physics-driven DRL environment that models the dynamics of a multi-fingered robotic hand. This environment is built upon a physics engine that captures the interactions between the hand and external objects, including rigid bodies, soft bodies, and deformable materials. We validate the environment's efficacy by demonstrating the training of a robotic hand to execute diverse tasks, such as object manipulation and navigation within complex settings. Furthermore, we illustrate the environment's utility by training a DRL agent to perform a novel, challenging task: navigating through a narrow corridor while simultaneously grasping and moving an object.

We report the detection of no potassium absorption in the atmosphere of the hot Jupiter WASP-31b, utilizing the UVES spectrograph on the ESO Very Large Telescope. This finding is based on a 10-hour observation campaign conducted on 2018 April 10, capturing the transit of the host star. The data were analyzed using the ESPaDOnS pipeline, which successfully reduced the spectra to a signal-to-noise ratio of 100 per pixel. Our results indicate that the abundance of potassium in WASP-31b's atmosphere is less than 10% of the solar value, a constraint that aligns with previous studies. This upper limit is consistent with theoretical predictions suggesting that potassium should have been depleted by the time the planet cooled to its current temperature.

Cloud-based High-Performance Computing-as-a-Service (HPCaaS) is becoming increasingly popular, yet it currently faces significant hurdles. A primary limitation is the necessity to restart and reinitialize applications after a session ends, a process that incurs substantial time delays and financial costs. This study introduces a novel architecture designed to mitigate these issues by leveraging Non-Volatile RAM (NVRAM) to persist application states across sessions. The proposed solution encompasses both a hardware infrastructure and a software framework. The hardware layer utilizes Intel's Optane DC Persistent Memory alongside Intel Xeon Scalable processors, while the software framework employs the Kubernetes container orchestration engine to automate the orchestration of state persistence. To validate this approach, we conducted experiments using the SLURM workload scheduler, demonstrating that our architecture can cut reinitialization times by up to 90% and reduce associated costs by as much as 70%.

Recent years have seen significant interest in applying machine learning to population-level functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) classification, a field that has seen the development of numerous methods. However, these approaches often overlook the inherent graph structure of fMRI data, which can be effectively leveraged to enhance classification performance. In this study, we introduce a contrastive graph learning framework designed to capture inter-regional correlations within fMRI datasets. Our method utilizes a graph convolutional network to generate node embeddings, which are then optimized through a contrastive learning process to maximize the similarity of embeddings from the same subject across different brain regions. Experimental results on two fMRI datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

This paper offers a concise overview of Gauss sums, highlighting their historical origins and connections to the history of mathematics. It begins with an exploration of Gauss sums in algebra, detailing their role in proving the fundamental theorem on roots of unity and their significance as the original source of class field theory. The text then examines Gauss sums in the context of topology, focusing on their application to three-dimensional manifolds.
